title: Supervising the search process produces reliable and generalizable information-seeking agents
abstractText: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are transforming web search by shifting from document ranking to synthesizing answers, and are increasingly deployed as autonomous agentic search systems that iteratively interact with external knowledge sources. Despite this progress, building effective search agents remains challenging because high-quality intermediate search steps are difficult to generate. Previous approaches have primarily relied on outcome supervision, rewarding agents only for producing correct final answers. This often leads to reward hacking and excessive dependence on parametric memory, limiting generalization to out-of-domain tasks. To address these limitations, we introduce RAG-Gym, a framework that shifts supervision from final answers to the search process itself. With RAG-Gym, we systematically investigate architecture design, parameter optimization, and action evaluation, identifying reasoning reflection as a critical capability for search agents. Building on this insight, we propose Re 2 Search++, a process-supervised agent that achieves substantial improvements on multi-hop information-seeking benchmarks, especially in out-of-domain settings. Performance gains are driven primarily by higher-quality search queries rather than answer optimization alone, and the learned search critics transfer across models, including proprietary LLMs. These findings show that supervising the search process produces more reliable and generalizable information-seeking agents.

title: Identifying Middle Paleolithic Residential Units Through the Spatial Organization of Combustion Structures at Abric Romaní (Barcelona, Spain)
abstractText: Abstract The habitual and controlled use of fire among Neanderthal groups, together with the residential use of caves and rock shelters, represents a major turning point in the emergence of Paleolithic camp bases. In Middle Paleolithic sites, the interrelation between shelter geomorphology, fire-use locations and activity areas has been interpreted as evidence of spatial organization. Hearths are, therefore, valuable for investigating site structure. The Abric Romaní offers an exceptional case study due to the preservation and extensive excavation strategy of numerous combustion structures across several archaeological units. This study analyses fire-use spatial organization in units Nb, Oa, Ob, P, Qa and R (ca. 60–54 ka) to explore how Neanderthals structured their living spaces. Using spatial statistical methods (i.e., covariate analysis, spatial modelling, and mark analysis), we evaluate the influence of distance from the back wall on fire-use location and distribution. We then isolate this effect to examine micro-scale patterns and compare the morphological and functional characteristics of combustion structures between wall-adjacent and wall-distanced sectors and across the archaeological sequence. Our findings show a relationship between fire-use locations and the back wall, defining preferential zones for fire placement. Fire use reflects a structured spatial zoning, separating combustion structures in sleeping and resting areas from those in communal activity areas. The morphology of combustion structures remained stable across units, while fire use varied flexibly within a stable spatial framework. Overall, these findings suggest that late Neanderthal occupations at Abric Romaní exhibited structured spatial cultural patterns comparable to those documented in modern hunter-gatherer campsites.

title: Localized Crystallization of Ce:YIG Thin Films on Si Using CO2 Laser Annealing for Integrated Nonreciprocal Photonic Device Applications
abstractText: Abstract Laser annealing (LA) has emerged as an effective method for localized crystallization of magneto-optical (MO) garnet thin films on semiconductor substrates. However, few studies have explored the crystallization and magneto-optical (MO) properties of cerium-substituted yttrium iron garnet (Ce:YIG, Ce1Y2Fe5O12) thin films for integrated photonic device applications using the LA technique. In this study, we provide a comprehensive investigation into the laser annealing of Ce:YIG films deposited on SiO2 substrates and silicon nitride photonic waveguides for integrated nonreciprocal photonic device applications. Garnet phase was successfully observed in films grown on SiO2/Si substrates and SiN waveguides with laser annealing of sputtered Ce:YIG films on top of a laser annealed Y3Fe5O12 seed layer. The magneto-optical (MO) properties of Ce:YIG films on oxidized Si substrates were found to be comparable to those prepared by rapid thermal annealing (RTA). A Mach–Zehnder Interferometer (MZI) type optical isolator based on Ce:YIG film on SiN was fabricated, exhibiting a saturation Faraday rotation of −2317.7 ± 94.8 deg/cm and propagation loss of 188.2 ± 16.5 dB/cm. Isolation ratio of 27.1 dB and insertion loss of 10.1 dB were achieved at 1552.7 nm wavelength.

title: Analisis Pengaruh Etika dalam Administrasi Publik terhadap Kualitas Pelayanan di Perkantoran Terpadu pada Disdukcapil Kota Malang
abstractText: Penelitian ini mengkaji keterkaitan antara penerapan etika administrasi publik dengan mutu layanan yang dirasakan masyarakat di Perkantoran Terpadu Dinas Kependudukan dan Pencatatan Sipil (Disdukcapil) Kota Malang. Etika aparatur bukan sekadar kewajiban normatif, melainkan faktor penentu yang membentuk kualitas interaksi antara birokrasi dengan warga. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan jenis studi kasus. Pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui wawancara semi-terstruktur, observasi non-partisipatif, serta dokumentasi, dengan informan mencakup Kepala Bidang Pelayanan Pencatatan Sipil dan dua pengguna layanan. Analisis data mengacu pada model interaktif Miles, Huberman, dan Saldana. Kerangka teori yang digunakan adalah model etika James H. Svara (duty, virtue, principle, consequence) untuk menganalisis perilaku aparatur, serta model SERVQUAL Parasuraman, Zeithaml, dan Berry (tangibles, reliability, responsiveness, assurance, empathy) untuk mengukur kualitas layanan. Temuan penelitian menunjukkan bahwa nilai-nilai etika seperti integritas, transparansi, dan tanggung jawab yang diterapkan aparatur berdampak nyata pada seluruh dimensi kualitas pelayanan. Instansi ini telah meraih predikat Pelayanan Prima (A) tingkat nasional, mengembangkan inovasi SIAPEL dan layanan inklusif D-CARDs. Namun, inkonsistensi sikap antar petugas, keterbatasan kapasitas SDM, gangguan infrastruktur digital, serta rendahnya literasi digital sebagian masyarakat masih menjadi hambatan yang memerlukan penanganan berkelanjutan.

title: Implementasi Good Governance Pada Pendidikan Sekolah Dasar Kota Malang
abstractText: Penelitian ini mengkaji implementasi prinsip-prinsip good governance berdasarkan kerangka United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) pada pendidikan sekolah dasar di Kota Malang. Tujuan penelitian adalah menganalisis penerapan tujuh prinsip good governance transparansi, akuntabilitas, partisipasi, rule of law, efektivitas dan efisiensi, responsivitas, serta visi strategis, sekaligus mengidentifikasi kendala dan merumuskan rekomendasi strategis. Metode yang digunakan adalah pendekatan kualitatif melalui teknik pengumpulan data berupa wawancara mendalam, observasi, dan studi literatur, dengan analisis data secara induktif menggunakan triangulasi metode dan sumber. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa SDN Kauman 1 telah menerapkan ketujuh prinsip tersebut pada tataran prosedural dengan komitmen yang nyata, namun tingkat implementasinya masih bervariasi dan belum sepenuhnya optimal. Transparansi telah diwujudkan melalui mekanisme komunikasi multi saluran, akuntabilitas dijalankan melalui sistem pelaporan berjenjang dan manajemen berbasis tim, sementara partisipasi orang tua difasilitasi melalui mitra kelas yang terbukti lebih efektif daripada komite sekolah formal. Disisi lain, terdapat sejumlah hambatan struktural yang signifikan, di antaranya inkonsistensi kebijakan pendidikan nasional, rigiditas sistem penganggaran ARKAS dan SIPD, kesenjangan antara regulasi dan kebutuhan tenaga pendidik, serta ketimpangan akses teknologi di kalangan peserta didik. Penelitian ini merekomendasikan sinergi antara penguatan kapasitas kelembagaan internal sekolah dan reformasi kebijakan pendidikan nasional yang lebih adaptif, kontekstual, dan konsisten demi terwujudnya tata kelola pendidikan dasar yang bermakna dan berkelanjutan.

title: Komunikasi Risiko Kebakaran Pada Fase Pra-Bencana Melalui Edukasi dan Simulasi Di Rumah Susun Sederhana Sewa (Rusunawa) Banda Aceh
abstractText: Kebakaran merupakan bencana nonalam yang umumnya dipicu oleh human error dan berpotensi menimbulkan korban jiwa serta kerugian ekonomi terutama pada hunian vertikal seperti Rumah Susun Sederhana Sewa (Rusunawa). Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis tingkat pengetahuan dan kesiapsiagaan penghuni Rusunawa terhadap kebakaran serta mengevaluasi komunikasi risiko melalui edukasi dan simulasi pada fase pra-bencana. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan deskriptif kuantitatif dengan observasi kualitatif di Rusunawa Peulanggahan Kota Banda Aceh melibatkan 51 responden. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan tingkat pengetahuan penghuni berada pada kategori cukup dengan rata-rata jawaban benar sebesar 55,5%. Pengetahuan mengenai bahaya kebakaran relatif baik namun aspek kelembagaan dan pengalaman mengikuti edukasi masih rendah. Komunikasi risiko melalui edukasi dan simulasi berkontribusi terhadap peningkatan pemahaman masyarakat tetapi penguatan kesiapsiagaan tetap memerlukan penyusunan SOP kebakaran, jalur evakuasi, tim tanggap darurat berbasis komunitas serta pelaksanaan edukasi dan simulasi secara berkala.

title: Evaluasi Kualitas Pelayanan Administrasi Kependudukan Berbasis E-Governance Melalui Aplikasi SIAPEL di Kelurahan Lowokwaru Kota Malang
abstractText: Pelayanan administrasi kependudukan merupakan salah satu layanan publik yang berperan penting dalam pemenuhan hak-hak sipil masyarakat. Seiring perkembangan teknologi informasi, pemerintah menerapkan konsep e-governance untuk meningkatkan kualitas pelayanan yang lebih efektif, efisien, transparan, dan akuntabel, salah satunya melalui aplikasi SIAPEL (Sistem Informasi Administrasi Pelayanan Elektronik) di Kelurahan Lowokwaru, Kota Malang. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengevaluasi kualitas pelayanan administrasi kependudukan melalui SIAPEL, mengidentifikasi faktor pendukung dan penghambat implementasinya, serta menganalisis kontribusinya terhadap peningkatan efektivitas pelayanan publik. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif dengan teknik pengumpulan data melalui wawancara, observasi, dan dokumentasi yang melibatkan lurah, operator SIAPEL, pegawai pelayanan, dan masyarakat pengguna layanan. Analisis data dilakukan menggunakan model Miles, Huberman, dan Saldaña. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa implementasi SIAPEL telah meningkatkan kualitas pelayanan administrasi kependudukan di Kelurahan Lowokwaru. Berdasarkan dimensi SERVQUAL, indikator reliability dan responsiveness menjadi aspek yang paling berpengaruh karena mampu mempercepat proses pelayanan, meningkatkan ketepatan administrasi, serta memperkuat respons petugas terhadap kebutuhan masyarakat. Sementara itu, aspek tangibles, assurance, dan empathy turut mendukung kualitas pelayanan melalui kemudahan penggunaan aplikasi, jaminan keamanan data, dan pendampingan bagi pengguna yang mengalami kesulitan dalam mengakses layanan digital. Keberhasilan implementasi SIAPEL didukung oleh komitmen pemerintah daerah, ketersediaan infrastruktur digital, koordinasi antar lembaga yang baik, serta meningkatnya penerimaan masyarakat terhadap layanan digital. Namun, implementasinya masih menghadapi kendala berupa rendahnya literasi digital sebagian masyarakat, keterbatasan kompetensi sumber daya manusia, dan gangguan jaringan internet. Secara keseluruhan, SIAPEL berhasil mendukung penerapan e-governance yang lebih efektif, efisien, transparan, dan akuntabel sehingga berpotensi menjadi model pelayanan administrasi kependudukan berbasis digital yang dapat direplikasi di berbagai daerah di Indonesia.

title: Analisis Kualitas Transportasi Publik Suroboyo Bus Berdasarkan Pengalaman Pengguna di Kota Surabaya
abstractText: Transportasi publik memiliki peran strategis dalam mendukung mobilitas masyarakat perkotaan sekaligus mengurangi kemacetan dan dampak negatif penggunaan kendaraan pribadi. Salah satu inovasi transportasi publik di Kota Surabaya adalah Suroboyo Bus yang menawarkan layanan transportasi modern dengan konsep ramah lingkungan melalui sistem pembayaran menggunakan sampah plastik. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis kualitas pelayanan Suroboyo Bus berdasarkan pengalaman pengguna. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif dengan teknik pengumpulan data berupa observasi, wawancara mendalam, dan dokumentasi. Analisis data dilakukan melalui tahapan reduksi data, penyajian data, dan penarikan kesimpulan. Kerangka analisis yang digunakan mengacu pada model SERVQUAL yang meliputi dimensi reliability, tangibles, responsiveness, assurance, dan empathy. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kualitas pelayanan Suroboyo Bus secara umum dinilai baik oleh pengguna. Aspek yang memperoleh penilaian positif meliputi kenyamanan dan kebersihan armada, keramahan petugas, keamanan perjalanan, serta kemudahan sistem pembayaran. Namun demikian, masih ditemukan beberapa kendala, seperti ketidakkonsistenan jadwal kedatangan bus, keterbatasan fasilitas halte, kurang optimalnya penyediaan informasi layanan secara real-time, serta kepadatan penumpang pada jam tertentu. Temuan penelitian menunjukkan bahwa peningkatan kualitas infrastruktur halte dan keandalan operasional perlu menjadi prioritas untuk meningkatkan kepuasan pengguna dan mendorong penggunaan transportasi publik secara berkelanjutan.

title: Hierarchical modeling of retailers' issues for lean dairy supply chain: a data-driven decision-making approach
abstractText: Purpose This research identifies key retailer-related issues causing inefficiencies in the Indian Dairy Supply Chain (DSC) and develops a hierarchical model aimed at guiding decision-makers towards a leaner and more productive DSC. The study addresses a significant gap in the lean DSC literature, focusing on the challenges retailers face in emerging markets such as India. Design/methodology/approach The study employs a mixed-method approach, beginning with a comprehensive literature review and expert consultations to identify 15 critical retailer issues. A structured questionnaire was administered to industry professionals and academics, resulting in 290 valid responses. Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) was applied to uncover underlying constructs, followed by Total Interpretive Structural Modeling (TISM) to map relationships among these issues. The model was statistically validated using a one-sample t-test, and MICMAC analysis classified issues by their driving power and dependence. Findings The study categorizes the identified retailer issues into four constructs: strategic, tactical, operational, and performance. Strategic issues (lack of top management commitment, insufficient financial support, and lack of assured long-term contracts) emerged as the most powerful drivers, underscoring their fundamental role in addressing other retailers' concerns. Tactical issues, including inadequate cold storage and ICT infrastructure, significantly influenced operational efficiency. Performance issues, such as retailer dissatisfaction, were the most dependent and were strongly influenced by strategic and tactical factors. Research limitations/implications The study specifically focuses on the Indian DSC, limiting generalizability to other geographical or sectoral contexts. Additionally, the findings depend heavily on expert input, which may introduce subjectivity. Future research could validate these findings through broader empirical studies and comparative analysis in other regions or industries to enhance generalizability and robustness. Practical implications The hierarchical model developed in this research provides clear prioritization guidelines for decision-makers and policymakers in the dairy industry. Strategic issues, notably management commitment and financial support, must be addressed first to resolve tactical and operational inefficiencies. Policymakers can use these insights to formulate targeted policies, invest strategically, and develop training and infrastructure programs that significantly enhance retailer performance and supply chain efficiency. Originality/value This study contributes to the lean DSC literature by systematically identifying and modeling retailer-level barriers and by integrating EFA, TISM, and MICMAC into a data-driven hierarchical framework. The findings extend existing knowledge on supply chain performance management by demonstrating how strategic-level factors shape tactical and operational outcomes at the retail node of dairy supply chains. The developed model provides a structured decision-support mechanism to improve operational performance, reduce waste, and strengthen performance management practices within the DSC.

title: Exploring psychological therapists’ perspectives and experiences of lifestyle psychiatry implementation: a qualitative study
abstractText: Abstract Background Lifestyle psychiatry emphasises the role of modifiable health behaviours such as sleep, diet, smoking cessation, and physical activity on mental health. Despite growing evidence, the integration of lifestyle psychiatry into standard mental health care remains limited. The views of psychological therapists on this integration are under researched. Aim To explore psychological therapists’ perspectives and experiences of incorporating lifestyle psychiatry into therapy. Methods Eighteen psychological therapists participated in semi-structured interviews, using reflexive thematic analysis to explore their experiences and perspectives on incorporating lifestyle psychiatry into therapy. Results Four overarching themes were developed: (1) Therapists’ conceptualisations of lifestyle; (2) The place of lifestyle in the therapy process; (3) Barriers to addressing lifestyle in therapy (4) Making it possible: facilitators and future directions. Conclusions Most therapists perceived lifestyle psychiatry as relevant and compatible with their current practice. However, structured guidance, training, and interdisciplinary collaboration were seen as necessary to embed lifestyle psychiatry into their work. Systemic changes addressing role ambiguity, service-level pressures, and client barriers may enable further integration of lifestyle psychiatry into clinical practice. title: Pengaruh Harga dan Kualitas Pelayanan terhadap Kepuasan Konsumen Pada Rumah Makan Geprek Uyat Kota Gorontalo
abstractText: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui dan menganalisis pengaruh harga dan kualitas pelayanan terhadap kepuasan konsumen pada Rumah Makan Geprek Uyat Cabang Kota Gorontalo, baik secara parsial maupun simultan. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain deskriptif kausal. Populasi penelitian adalah konsumen yang melakukan pembelian pada outlet Jl. Padang dan Wongkaditi. Sampel berjumlah 100 responden yang ditentukan dengan teknik accidental sampling dan rumus Cochran. Data dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner, observasi, dan wawancara, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan regresi linear berganda yang didukung uji validitas, reliabilitas, asumsi klasik, uji t, uji F, dan koefisien determinasi. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa harga berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap kepuasan konsumen, kualitas pelayanan berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap kepuasan konsumen, serta harga dan kualitas pelayanan secara simultan berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap kepuasan konsumen. Model penelitian menjelaskan 30,1% variasi kepuasan konsumen, sedangkan 69,9% dijelaskan oleh faktor lain di luar model. Implikasi penelitian menunjukkan pentingnya mempertahankan harga yang wajar dan kompetitif serta meningkatkan kualitas pelayanan secara berkelanjutan.

title: Analisis Word of Mouth, Iklan Online, dan Brand Image terhadap Kepuasan Pelanggan melalui Keputusan Pembelian PT Levarian Aromaindo Pratama
abstractText: This study examines the effects of Word of Mouth, Online Advertising, and Brand Image on Purchase Decision and Customer Satisfaction at PT Levarian Aromaindo Pratama, and the role of Purchase Decision as a link to Customer Satisfaction. A quantitative approach was employed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with bootstrapping. The findings show that Word of Mouth positively influences Purchase Decision (β = 0.129; p = 0.006), as does Online Advertising (β = 0.173; p = 0.003), while Brand Image demonstrates the strongest effect (β = 0.660; p < 0.001). These variables explain 61.7% of Purchase Decision. Word of Mouth and Online Advertising have no direct effect on Customer Satisfaction, whereas Brand Image has a significant negative effect (β = −0.187; p = 0.023). Purchase Decision positively influences Customer Satisfaction (β = 0.771; p < 0.001), with the model explaining 40.3% of its variance. The indirect effects of all three marketing factors through Purchase Decision are significant. These findings indicate that marketing communication and brand perceptions guide consumers toward purchase decisions that subsequently contribute to satisfaction. The study contributes to marketing research by integrating these factors within one empirical model linking pre-purchase influences with post-purchase evaluation

title: Residual Finite Group Element Dandelion-Informed Attention Network for Symbolic Knowledge Integration in AI-Driven Educational Intelligence
abstractText: Recent advances in intelligent educational systems have emphasized the need for accurate interpretation of Computational Thinking (CT) behaviors. The contextual dependencies and symbolic reasoning necessary to comprehend CT in game-based learning environments are frequently difficult for traditional deep learning techniques to capture. This disparity draws attention to the issue of the current models of educational analytics’ poor generalization and interpretability. The current study presents a novel framework called the Residual Finite Group Element Dandelion Informed Attention Network (Res-FGE-DIAN) under the paradigm of AI in Education with Symbolic Knowledge Integration in order to address this challenge. The proposed framework analyzes CT behaviors using game-based interaction data named “Educational Testing Service (ETS) and Educational Knowledge” dataset, which consists of 427 player records from the AutoThinking learning game. The Masked Attention Mask Transformer (Mask2Former) was used to extract features for improved contextual encoding, and the Cumulative Curve Fitting Approximation (CCFA) algorithm was used for data pre-processing in order to normalize and refine the learning traces. The Res-FGE-DIAN combines a Residual Group Attention Network (ResGANet) and a Finite-Element-Informed Neural Network (FEI-NN), both of which are optimized using the Dandelion Optimizer (DO) to guarantee effective convergence and stability. Symbolic representation and decision accuracy are further improved by supporting architectures, such as the Residual Finite Group Element Dandelion Informed Attention Network (RES-FGE-DIAN). The suggested model predicts and interprets learners’ CT performance with 99.9% accuracy, according to experimental validation.

title: Fatigue response of pre-corroded chromic-acid-anodized AA7050-T7451 and phase-field analysis of stress-dependent localized dissolution
abstractText: Abstract Understanding the effects of environmental exposure and cyclic loading on localized damage is important for assessing the fatigue performance of anodized aluminium. This study investigates the fatigue response of chromic-acid-anodized AA7050-T7451 and the stress-dependent evolution of localized corrosion. Cyclic-immersion and intermittent-salt-fog exposures were followed by mass-loss measurements, microscopic observations and axial fatigue testing in laboratory air at R = 0.06. Small average mass losses coexisted with localized surface changes and appreciable fatigue-life scatter. At 180 MPa, the cyclic-immersion groups exhibited sample mean fatigue lives 57.1–73.6% below the uncorroded reference, with a non-monotonic dependence on exposure duration. Increasing the maximum nominal stress from 180 to 200 MPa reduced the mean fatigue life by 22.0–45.9% at the same cyclic-immersion durations. A two-dimensional displacement–phase-field–concentration model examined localized dissolution under cyclic loading for initial cavity depths of 0.01 and 0.02 mm. Higher cyclic stress promoted local plastic deformation and increased interface mobility, accelerating inward dissolution. At 900 s, increasing the maximum nominal stress from 160 to 240 MPa increased total defect depth by 45.2–51.2%, whereas lateral width changed by no more than 2.2%. At 240 MPa and 900 s, the larger initial cavity developed 45.8% greater additional penetration, demonstrating the influence of initial geometry on subsequent damage evolution. These findings provide a mechanistic explanation for stress-enhanced localized corrosion and highlight the importance of considering exposure history, loading conditions and initial defect geometry jointly in the fatigue assessment of anodized aluminium.

title: Sarcosine-Mediated Interface Regulation of SnO2 Electron Transport Layer toward High-Performance and Durable MAPbI3 Perovskite Solar Cells
abstractText: Abstract Driven by exceptional light-to-electricity conversion performance alongside inexpensive solution-phase manufacturing, metal halide perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have emerged as a major focus of next-generation photovoltaic research. Nevertheless, further performance enhancements remain constrained by high defect densities at the electron transport layer (ETL) interface, suboptimal band alignment, and pronounced nonradiative carrier recombination. Herein, a direct incorporation strategy was developed by introducing sarcosine (Sar) into the SnO2 colloidal precursor to regulate the surface properties and chemical environment of the SnO2 electron transport layer, which is associated with improved MAPbI3 perovskite film formation. Spectroscopic characterizations indicate that chemical coordination between the amine/carboxylic moieties of Sar and unsaturated Sn centers at the SnO2 boundary contributes to interfacial defect passivation alongside a favorable energy band alignment. Simultaneously, the boosted surface hydrophilicity promotes uniform precursor coverage and regulates grain nucleation, ultimately yielding perovskite thin films with elevated crystalline order and minimized defect density. Consequently, optoelectronic analyses reveal accelerated interfacial charge transfer and suppressed nonradiative recombination pathways, contributing to reduced hysteresis and significantly improved photovoltaic performance. A champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 21.33% is achieved, compared with 18.72% for the control device. In addition, the Sar-modified solar cells exhibit superior operational robustness under continuous light exposure alongside prolonged shelf life stability in unencapsulated ambient air. Overall, this study presents a straightforward yet potent interface modification approach for constructing high-performance, durable MAPbI3 perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Functional Evaluation of the Reconstructed Bladder: Evolving Role of Urodynamics and Beyond
A MODEL STREPTOZOTOCIN MICE FOR STUDYING TYPE 2 DIABETES
abstractText: Animal models are always necessary in pathological research, especially for type 2 diabetes (T2D). It is a chronic metabolic disorder with a high rate of increasing and involves many physiological systems. This study aims to provide a chemically induced type 2 diabetes mouse model by administering streptozotocin (STZ). Adult Swiss Albino mice were divided into three main groups to inject different dosages of STZ, specifically low dose, high dose 1, and high dose 2. As a result, mice in the high-dose group with a total of 160 mg/kg STZ for two injections were considered to obtain type 2 diabetes. After 4 months of experiment, the mice did not lose weight and acted normally. Characteristic metabolic alterations in type 2 diabetes contained an average fasting blood sugar level of over 150 mg/dL, fatty liver, damaged kidneys, and HbA1c levels of over 6.5%. It can be said that this research is the initial basic step to developing an effective type 2 diabetes mouse model in the future.

title: Evidence map for treatment outcomes and prognostic determinants in periprosthetic joint infection: an umbrella review
abstractText: Abstract Background The reporting of outcomes following treatment for periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) suffers from inconsistent terminology and methodological constraints, complicating the interpretation of prognostic factors and treatment efficacy. This umbrella review synthesized systematic reviews and meta-analyses to evaluate the burden, comparative effectiveness, and prognostic factors associated with adverse PJI outcomes. Methods Following PRISMA guidelines, a comprehensive search of Cochrane Library, Embase, PubMed, and Web of Science was conducted from inception to April 20, 2026. We included meta-analyses reporting quantitative post-treatment outcomes for PJI. Methodological quality, risk of bias, and evidence certainty were assessed using AMSTAR-2, ROBIS, and GRADE, respectively. Evidence signals were stratified to separate comparative and prognostic associations from descriptive outcome-burden estimates. Results 53 reviews were included, predominantly assessing hip (THA) and knee (TKA) PJI. The overall certainty of evidence was generally low. PJI demonstrated a high descriptive outcome burden: across variable follow-up periods, overall pooled mortality was 11.0% after THA PJI and 13.3% after TKA PJI. The pooled failure rate for debridement, antibiotics, and implant retention (DAIR) was 35.9%, escalating to 73.6% in late chronic cases. Following one-stage revision, all-cause revision rates were 11.1% (THA) and 11.8% (TKA). These pooled burden estimates should be interpreted descriptively when follow-up durations differed across source reviews. Prognostically, several adverse associations were identified, including positive culture at two-stage reimplantation (OR = 1.92), obesity (OR up to 3.63 in TKA), and smoking (RR = 1.84), although the certainty and replication of these associations varied across evidence sources. Conclusion PJI carries a substantial burden of mortality and treatment failure. Available evidence identifies associations between adverse outcomes and host vulnerabilities, microbiological factors, treatment context, and surgical timing, although these relationships remain largely based on observational evidence rather than demonstrated causal mechanisms. Future research must prioritize standardized outcome definitions and prospective designs to clarify comparative treatment effects and improve individualized risk stratification.

title: Calcium Alginate/Polyaniline-PSS Core–Shell Particles: Synthesis and Multi-Mechanism Water Vapor Adsorption Behavior
abstractText: Abstract Core–shell composite particles combining a calcium alginate (Alg-Ca) hydrogel core with a polyaniline/polystyrene sulfonic acid (PANi/PSS) conductive polymer shell were synthesized and evaluated for water vapor adsorption applications. The resulting particles exhibited a well-defined, phase-separated architecture, comprising a highly hydrated, porous hydrogel core encapsulated by a structurally and chemically distinct shell, consistent with successful incorporation of the sulfonated conductive polymer onto the surface of the alginate network. The core and shell regions displayed markedly different thermal decomposition behavior, confirming their compositional distinction and demonstrating that the composite retains thermal stability within the operating range typical of gas-sensing applications. Kinetic analysis of water vapor adsorption as a function of relative humidity (RH, 50–95%) and temperature (25–45 °C) revealed a systematic transition among pseudo-first-order, pseudo-second-order, and Elovich kinetic models. At moderate RH, adsorption was governed by chemically homogeneous interactions at polar functional groups, while at near-saturation RH, the mechanism shifted toward multilayer adsorption and capillary condensation. Temperature-dependent measurements at fixed RH further revealed an unusual diffusion–reaction–diffusion transition across the studied temperature range. Across three adsorption–regeneration cycles, adsorption capacity increased progressively while the dominant kinetic model at each condition remained unchanged, indicating that regeneration preserves the fundamental water–material interaction mechanism while increasing the number of accessible active sites. These findings establish Alg-Ca@PANI–PSS as a structurally robust, reusable, and mechanistically well-characterized composite for humidity-responsive and gas-sensing applications.

title: Neurosurgical software device safety in the US: analysis of 2017–2025 FDA Recall and Adverse Event Data
abstractText: OBJECTIVE Neurosurgeons rely on multiple software applications for surgical planning, intraoperative navigation, and neurophysiological monitoring. Combined with the proliferation of AI-based clinical adjuncts, software as a medical device (SaMD) represents an evolving frontier with profound implications for patient safety. The aim of this study was to systematically analyze all software-related neurological medical device recalls initiated in the US from 2017 to 2025 and to assess the implications of recalls and adverse events for software devices currently in use, as well as the risks posed by emerging software platforms. METHODS Recall and adverse event information related to neurological SaMDs (2017–2025) was extracted from the FDA recall, MAUDE, AccessGUDID, and openFDA databases. Product codes were identified using the FDA Product Classification database. Associated adverse event data were extracted using a custom Python script with the openFDA application programming interface. RESULTS There were 20 unique software-associated neurological device recalls identified across 7 medical device companies and 4 distinct device categories, namely surgical navigation (55%), neurophysiological monitoring devices (25%), surgical planning (15%), and stereotactic devices (5%). More than half of the neurological devices that were recalled had FDA class I severity. Recalls categorized as class I displayed a significant upward trend in annual frequency from 2017 to 2024 (p = 0.027). The median recall times were shorter for class I versus class II recalls (4 vs 10 years, IQR 2–7 vs 6–11 years; Mann-Whitney U = 28, p = 0.182). There were 16,333 adverse event notifications, with 93.4% related to malfunction and 5.9% related to injury. Two surgical navigation devices alone were responsible for 88.8% of all documented adverse events. There was a significantly higher rate of severe adverse harm reported among class II than class I recalls (14.6% vs 3.6%, p < 0.001). More than 10,000 adverse events were reported after formal recall notification for two medical devices. System instability (55.0%) and software defects (43.5%) comprised 98.5% of adverse event notifications. CONCLUSIONS Device recalls and adverse events associated with neurological SaMDs trended toward greater severity of harm, were concentrated in a few high-throughput platforms, and generated a significant volume of adverse events that persisted even after the recall procedure took effect. The observed discordance between recall class and reported patient harm, as well as the prevalence of runtime instability as the most common software failure mode, represent potential areas of improvement for current regulatory frameworks. Adaptation by regulatory bodies and vigilance by providers is critical, particularly for identifying SaMD-related adverse events.

title: Turning values into value: the role of ethical climate and CAPS mediated and moderated mechanisms in fostering service innovation in hospitality
abstractText: Purpose This study investigates how ethical climate influences frontline service innovative behavior (SIB) through dual cognitive–affective personality system (CAPS) pathways: creative self-efficacy (CSE) and sense of belonging (SOB). Obsessive–compulsive tendencies (OCT) are examined as a boundary condition. Design/methodology/approach Two multi-wave, time-lagged studies were conducted with Malaysian hospitality employees (Study 1: N = 370; Study 2: N = 352), analyzed using PLS-SEM. Findings Across both studies, ethical climate positively predicted SIB directly and indirectly through CSE and SOB. In Study 2, OCT differentially moderated the two pathways: it strengthened the CSE–SIB relationship but weakened the SOB–SIB relationship. Evidence for conditional indirect effects was more limited and is therefore interpreted cautiously. Practical implications The findings show that hospitality organizations can encourage service innovation by supporting fairness, transparency and inclusion. It is also important to consider that employees' personalities may affect how they use their psychological resources to be innovative. Originality/value The present research advances the fields of hospitality ethics and innovation by examining dual cognitive and affective pathways through two time-lagged studies and presenting evidence from a non-Western service context.

title: Delivery-related road traffic crashes among food delivery riders in six Chinese cities: a multicentre cross-sectional study
abstractText: Abstract Food delivery riders are a rapidly growing workforce in urban China and are exposed to road traffic injury risks during daily work. Multicity evidence on delivery-related road traffic crashes in this population remains limited. We conducted a cross-sectional survey among 2,386 food delivery riders registered on the Meituan or Eleme platforms in six Chinese cities: Hefei, Jinan, Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Shantou, and Nanning. Data were collected on sociodemographic characteristics, work-related conditions, road safety knowledge, attitudes and behaviours, and self-reported delivery-related road traffic crashes in the past year. The overall prevalence of delivery-related road traffic crashes was 13.83%, with marked variation across cities, ranging from 6.85% in Shantou to 21.38% in Hefei. In bivariate analyses, crash involvement differed by selected sociodemographic and work-related characteristics, including marital status, monthly income, regular vehicle maintenance, work experience, daily order volume, and daily delivery distance. These findings describe multicity patterns of delivery-related road traffic crashes among food delivery riders and highlight areas for future injury prevention research, including workload management, vehicle maintenance, rider training, and traffic safety practices.

title: Rapid Fear Detection Predicts Prosocial Giving
abstractText: Abstract Prosociality is fundamental to human social life, yet individuals vary widely in their willingness to incur costs for others. What drives this variation? We tested four preregistered hypotheses about whether the speed of detecting specific social stimuli (faces vs. cars, infant vs. elderly faces, fearful vs. angry faces, trustworthy vs. untrustworthy faces) is associated with prosocial giving. Participants (N = 200) completed visual detection tasks, personality assessments, a Director Task measuring Theory of Mind, and two economic games: the Dictator Game, indexing costly giving in the absence of strategic pressure, and the Ultimatum Game, indexing giving under strategic constraints. One hypothesis received partial support: faster detection of fearful faces was associated with greater giving, an effect that was most robust in the Dictator Game and was significant in the primary analyses. Robustness checks confirmed the Dictator Game finding across analytic approaches, while the Ultimatum Game effect was attenuated in analyses using robust standard errors and ordinal logistic regression. Neither detection of other social stimuli, Big Five personality traits, facial width-to-height ratio, nor Theory of Mind performance reliably predicted giving. These findings suggest that absolute speed of detecting distress signals reliably predicted prosocial giving, that this effect did not reflect general processing speed, and that general social attunement, vulnerability sensitivity, and higher-order social cognition did not reliably predict giving.

title: NGHIÊN CỨU BÀO CHẾ PHIM DIPHENHYDRAMIN HYDROCLORID 12,5mg RÃ NHANH TẠI KHOANG MIỆNG BẰNG PHƯƠNG PHÁP ĐỔ KHUÔN DUNG MÔI
abstractText: Mục tiêu: Bào chế phim rã nhanh tại khoang miệng (OFDF) chứa diphenhydramin hydroclorid (DPH) 12,5mg bằng phương pháp đổ khuôn dung môi. Phương pháp nghiên cứu: Nghiên cứu thực nghiệm in vitro. Phim DPH được bào chế bằng phương pháp đổ khuôn dung môi. Khảo sát ảnh hưởng của dung môi, polyme tạo phim, kích thước phim và chất hóa dẻo đến đặc tính của chế phẩm. Phim được đánh giá về các chỉ tiêu chất lượng, độ hòa tan và đặc tính lý hóa bằng phổ hồng ngoại (FTIR), phân tích nhiệt vi sai (DSC), nhiễu xạ tia X (XRD). Kết quả: Công thức sử dụng Hydroxypropyl Methylcellulose (HPMC) E15, Polyethylene glycol (PEG) 400 và glycerine tạo phim trong suốt, nhẵn, độ bền gấp > 350 lần, độ dày khoảng 100µm và thời gian rã < 30 giây. Hàm lượng DPH đạt yêu cầu; > 70% dược chất được giải phóng sau 5 phút và gần hoàn toàn sau 15 phút. Kết quả FTIR, DSC và XRD cho thấy DPH chủ yếu ở trạng thái vô định hình và không có tương tác đáng kể với tá dược. Teaching Biorefinery Concepts: From Waste Red Pine Sawdust to Regenerated Cellulose
abstractText: Abstract The integration of strategies for industrial waste valorization into education is a highly topical topic. This helps to prepare professionals who are capable of addressing current environmental and economic challenges. However, its integration into experimentally driven undergraduate experiences remains limited, particularly in multidisciplinary programs with a minimal chemistry focus. In this work, we present a laboratory experiment for undergraduate students focused on producing a cellulose thread fromPinus sylvestris biomass. Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) are used as fractionation solvents and a technology similar to Lyocell for cellulose solubilization and regeneration. By using regional agroforestry waste biomass, students gain both deep discipline-specific knowledge and interdisciplinary skills to address complex human-environment interactions. This approach emphasizes biorefinery concepts, enabling students to explore new waste valorization processes while fostering awareness of energy challenges, climate change causes, and sustainable development goals (SDGs). The activity equips students to drive societal changes that protect the environment and improve the quality of life.

Analysis of Pressure Differential and Smoke-Blocking Air Velocity of Vestibule Smoke Control Systems in a High-Rise Building Using CONTAM
abstractText: Pressurized smoke control systems in high-rise buildings are affected by vertical shafts, leakage characteristics, and stack effects. In this study, CONTAM was used to examine the pressure differential and smoke-blocking air velocity of a vestibular smoke control system under normal and winter conditions. Under normal conditions, relatively high pressure differentials were observed in several basement smoke control zones. The modification of the exhaust air path reduced these values to approximately 46-60 Pa. On the upper floors, smoke-blocking air velocities ranged from 0.83 to 0.93 m/s. During winter, the neutral pressure level was estimated to be near the 12th floor, with pressure differentials increasing at higher elevations. Under the building and analysis conditions considered in this study, smoke control performance was found to vary considerably with building height and pressure distribution, indicating the need to evaluate the system over the full height of the building.

title: The precarity trap: Modelling longitudinal trajectories of precarious youth employment and associations with mental health in the Australian HILDA Survey
abstractText: Abstract Background Early employment experiences are an important determinant of health and wellbeing in later adulthood. However, research on the mental health impacts of precarious employment has largely focused on older working-age adults, with limited attention paid to the consequences of employment precarity in young people under the age of 25. This study aimed to identify longitudinal trajectories of precarious employment during emerging adulthood (18–24 years) and examine associations with short- and long-term mental health outcomes. Methods Group-based trajectory modelling and adjusted linear/logistic regressions were applied to panel data from the nationally representative Household, Income and Labour Dynamics in Australia (HILDA) Survey. The analytic sample ( n = 498; person-year observations = 5,856) included participants employed between ages 18–24, with mental health measured at 25 and 35 years using the Mental Health Inventory-Five Item (MHI-5). Informed by a lived experience youth advisory group, employment precarity was measured with subjective survey items capturing perceived job security and job control. Results Two distinct trajectories of precarious employment were identified: persistent high precarity and low and decreasing precarity . Overall, persistent high precarity was associated with poorer mental health at age 25, particularly for females. By age 35, distinct sex differences emerged. For the job security dimension, males in persistent high precarity trajectories exhibited significantly poorer mental health compared to females. Conversely, females had significantly poorer mental health at 35 for persistent low job control. Conclusions These findings demonstrate that early and chronic employment precarity is associated with poorer short- and long-term mental health and suggest sex-specific pathways of vulnerability to different aspects of precarity. Policymakers and employers can help to safeguard the current and future mental health of young Australians by promoting secure and supportive working conditions.

title: Sosialisasi Pencegahan dan Penanggulangan Kekerasan Seksual di Lingkungan SMA Negeri 1 Bonegunu Kabupaten Buton Utara
abstractText: Kekerasan seksual di satuan pendidikan terus meningkat; pada semester pertama 2026, 78% dari 55 kasus kekerasan di sekolah yang dicatat Federasi Serikat Guru Indonesia merupakan kekerasan seksual. Mitra kegiatan, SMA Negeri 1 Bonegunu, Kabupaten Buton Utara, menghadapi dua persoalan: kurangnya pengetahuan warga sekolah mengenai ketentuan pidana dalam Undang-Undang Nomor 12 Tahun 2022 tentang Tindak Pidana Kekerasan Seksual (UU TPKS) dan belum dipahaminya strategi pencegahan serta penanggulangannya. Kegiatan ini bertujuan meningkatkan pemahaman dan kesadaran hukum siswa mengenai bentuk kekerasan seksual, ancaman pidananya, serta langkah pencegahan dan penanggulangannya. Kegiatan dilaksanakan pada 8 Juni 2026 oleh tim Fakultas Hukum Universitas Halu Oleo melalui tahap pra pelaksanaan, pelaksanaan, dan evaluasi dengan metode ceramah interaktif dan tanya jawab. Materi mencakup sembilan jenis tindak pidana kekerasan seksual, pelecehan seksual fisik dan nonfisik beserta ancaman pidananya, pemberatan pidana, serta strategi preventif dan represif. Hasil evaluasi melalui observasi dan tanya jawab menunjukkan bahwa peserta mampu membedakan kekerasan seksual fisik dan psikis, pelecehan, dan perkosaan, serta mengetahui upaya hukum yang dapat ditempuh; keterlibatan peserta terlihat dari pertanyaan yang diajukan sejak awal hingga akhir kegiatan. Kegiatan lanjutan perlu dilengkapi pre-test dan post-test serta pendampingan penyusunan mekanisme pengaduan di sekolah.

title: Advancing value creation in B2B market research – a human–AI collaboration framework for large language model
abstractText: Purpose This study aims to examine how prompt design influences the quality of large language model (LLM)-generated business-to-business (B2B) market research outputs. It also proposes a switch-point governance mechanism for converting LLM-generated drafts into decision-ready market intelligence artefacts. Design/methodology/approach The study uses an exploratory pilot evaluation of three market-facing LLM-based tools: ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity AI. The tools are compared across three benchmark B2B market research tasks and three prompt types: basic, context-augmented and role-specific. In total, 81 outputs were generated. A role-specific benchmark subset of 27 outputs was then assessed using automated metrics and blinded human ratings. The automated metrics included relevance through cosine similarity, reference overlap through ROUGE-F1, cross-run semantic stability, latency, token length and readability through Flesch Reading Ease. Human evaluators rated the outputs on relevance, completeness, factuality, instruction-following and insightfulness. One-way ANOVA and non-parametric checks are reported as exploratory task-level tests, not as confirmatory evidence of model superiority. Findings Role-specific prompts produced the strongest descriptive scores in this pilot setting. Within the benchmark subset, Gemini showed the strongest observed profile, with higher average relevance, reference overlap and semantic stability, along with lower latency. ChatGPT produced relevant outputs but tended to generate longer and less readable drafts. Perplexity generated concise and readable summaries, but its outputs were less aligned with the reference brief and decision-facing requirements. Human ratings followed a similar descriptive pattern. Cross-run semantic stability showed directional alignment with higher decision-readiness ratings, offering preliminary support for P1. The proposed switch-point matrix illustrates P2 by mapping automated confidence signals and human judgement to four escalation actions: accept, judge, review/redo and rewrite. Research limitations/implications The study is an exploratory pilot case. The task set is small, and the task-level ANOVA is based on only three observations per tool. The findings may also vary across domains, model versions, prompt libraries and organisational contexts. Future research should expand the task bank, include more B2B sectors, use larger rater pools, compare additional model versions and test the switch-point thresholds in live market intelligence workflows. Practical implications The study provides a replicable workflow for B2B market intelligence teams. It shows how teams can standardise prompt design, screen LLM-generated outputs, combine automated checks with human evaluation and allocate decision rights through transparent escalation rules. Social implications The framework supports accountable use of LLM-based market research by reducing the risk that persuasive but weakly grounded claims enter managerial decision-making. It also highlights the need for human oversight; evidence checks and traceable governance in AI-supported knowledge work. Originality/value The study extends service-dominant logic to LLM-mediated B2B market research by treating LLM outputs as candidate value propositions rather than finished knowledge products. Its main contribution is the operationalisation of decision-rights governance through cross-run semantic stability and switch-point logic.

title: Metabolic and hormonal responses to nutritional ketosis across metabolic phenotypes and sex in adults
abstractText: Abstract Ketogenic diets are increasingly used for weight management and metabolic improvement, but it remains unclear whether nutritional ketosis induces uniform adaptation across metabolic phenotypes and sex. This exploratory study examined phenotype- and sex-dependent responses to a 60-day ketogenic diet in adults with normal weight, overweight or obesity. Participants were stratified into six metabolic phenotype–sex groups and assessed at baseline, day 14, day 30 and day 60. Plasma biochemical and hormonal markers, appetite and perceived stress scores, and body composition were analyzed using repeated-measures models. During the ketogenic diet intervention, β-hydroxybutyrate increased in all groups, confirming nutritional ketosis, but the response differed between groups and was most progressive in men with obesity. Free fatty acids manifested in a heterogeneous manner, exhibiting distinct time-, phenotype-, and sex-dependent profiles. Glucose decreased after diet initiation, whereas insulin and HOMA-IR improved mainly in participants with overweight and obesity. Lipid profile changes were variable, while liver enzymes showed a sex-dependent temporal pattern. Appetite score differed by metabolic phenotype, leptin changed according to phenotype and sex, and ghrelin remained unchanged. Self-reported perceived stress scores showed group-specific changes, whereas cortisol changed over time and body mass, fat mass, visceral adipose tissue and subcutaneous adipose tissue decreased. These findings indicate that responses observed during the ketogenic diet intervention showed variable patterns across metabolic phenotypes and sex; however, given the limited sample size, these apparent between-group differences should be interpreted cautiously. Because of the single-arm design, these changes cannot be attributed to nutritional ketosis independently of weight loss or changes in energy intake.

title: Zika-Related Microcephaly in the First 5 Years After Birth
abstractText: OBJECTIVE To characterize clinical manifestations and complications of children with Zika-related microcephaly in the first 5 years after birth. METHODS A cohort of children with Zika-related microcephaly were observed up to age 60 months as part of the Microcephaly Epidemic Research Group Pediatric Cohort. RESULTS Among the 181 children, 43.1% were male and 77.2% were born at term. The median birth weight was 2700 g, with 64.8% classified as small for gestational age. Notably, 22.3% were diagnosed with microcephaly after birth, and 48.8% had severe microcephaly. Most common phenotypic characteristics were craniofacial disproportion (54.1%), arthrogryposis (35.9%), and exacerbated occipital protuberance (35.5%). Approximately one-third (33.1%) presented with dysphagia (n = 151 evaluated at median age of 28.2 months), and 13.3% of children had gastrostomies (median age of 24 months). Hearing anomalies were detected in 9.7% (n = 93 evaluated at median age of 30 months). In ophthalmological evaluation, 30.4% showed changes in the retina and 28.5% in the optic nerve; strabismus was observed in 53.4%. During neurological assessment (median age at first assessment of 15.9 months), 73.8% presented with abnormalities. Imaging examinations showed ventriculomegaly and cortical atrophy in 75.3% and 64.4% of the children, respectively. Electroencephalography was performed based on clinical indication in 84 children, of whom 92.9% had pattern alterations. Over the 5 years, 62.4% were hospitalized, mainly for respiratory problems and seizures. CONCLUSIONS The study highlights the severity of Zika-related microcephaly. Future research should prioritize continued systematic monitoring of these children to understand the frequency and timing of late-onset manifestations and complications, including death.

title: Rigid Tröger’s Base-Containing Poly( p -terphenyl pyridine) Membranes with Enlarged Free Volume and Robust Mechanical Strength for High-Temperature Proton-Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells
abstractText: Abstract The plasticizing effect of phosphoric acid seriously deteriorates the mechanical properties of high-temperature proton-exchange membranes and hinders the practical application of fuel cells. Herein, we synthesize two Tröger’s base-containing aromatic monomers with tunable rigidity (named DMD and TMD) to prepare copolymers based on poly(p-terphenyl pyridine) (PTP). The proposed poly(p-terphenyl pyridine-co-TMD, PTPT) membrane presents a narrower micropore size and a higher micropore density than the original PTP membrane, as evidenced by the CO2 adsorption isotherm. The highly rigid and twisted structure of TMD endows the PTPT membrane with increased free volume and improved mechanical strength to counteract the plasticizing effect of the doped phosphoric acid (PA). The PTPT membrane doped with 276 wt % PA displays a volume swelling ratio of 121%, which is lower than that of 162% for the PTP membrane doping with 223 wt % PA. Moreover, this PA-doped PTPT membrane delivers an anhydrous proton conductivity of 139 mS cm–1 at 160 °C, which is higher than that of the PA-doped PTP membrane (99 mS cm–1). Besides the high PA doping level, the increased proton conductivity benefits from the formation of larger and well-connected ion transport channels within the PTPT membrane, as proved by SAXS profiles and AFM adhesion force images. The PA-doped PTPT membrane-based H2/O2 fuel cell demonstrates a peak power density of 1116 mW cm–2 at 180 °C under a Pt loading of 1.0 mg cm–2 without humidity or backpressure. When 1 bar backpressure is applied to both the anode and the cathode, the fuel cell delivers a peak power density of 1600 mW cm–2 at 180 °C under a Pt loading of 0.6 mg cm–2 corresponding to a specific power of 2667 mW mg–1. Additionally, the PTPT-membrane-based fuel cell works stably during start/stop cycling for hundreds of times.

Comparative Analysis of Domestic and International Fire Safety Regulations for Logistics Facilities Based on Fire Damage Characteristics
abstractText: This study analyzed the fire risk characteristics of logistics facilities in Korea and compared domestic fire safety regulations with those of the United States, the United Kingdom, Japan, and Singapore. Major fire cases since 2020 and warehouse fire statistics from 2021 to 2025 were reviewed. Because logistics facilities are not independently classified in national fire statistics, warehouse fire statistics, which include logistics facilities, were used to examine fire and damage trends. During the five-year period, 6,596 warehouse fires occurred, and the annual fire frequency remained relatively stable. In contrast, property damage varied substantially, depending on the large-scale fire events. Carelessness and electrical factors accounted for 72.7% of all fires. Major fire cases commonly involved large storage spaces, high-density combustible storage, rack and multi-tier configurations, and prolonged firefighting. The international comparison showed that foreign regulations more actively reflect commodity hazards, storage heights, internal configurations, and operational changes in fire safety requirements. These results suggest that Korean regulations should incorporate actual storage and operational characteristics into existing fire safety frameworks.

title: Bedas Digital Services as an E-Government Instrument in Population Administration: A Literature Review
abstractText: This study examines the implementation of Bedas Digital Service (BDS) in Bandung Regency and identifies priorities for improving digital population administration services. A qualitative library research approach was adopted, drawing on scientific articles, books, regulations, policy documents, and official government publications. The collected information was examined using descriptive and thematic content analysis. During April–December 2024, BDS recorded 75,370 registered accounts and 278,706 service requests, including 178,175 non-booking requests and 100,531 Kartu Tanda Penduduk/KTP printing bookings. The synthesis identified four priorities: strengthening system and network reliability, improving cross-institutional data interoperability, developing human resource capacity, and expanding digital literacy and inclusive access. The reported figures indicate substantial platform utilization but do not independently demonstrate service effectiveness. Optimizing BDS requires coordinated improvements in technology, institutional processes, and citizens’ ability to access digital services. Reliance on secondary sources prevents direct assessment of platform performance, service quality, and user experiences. The findings therefore require validation through primary empirical research. This study contributes to e-government literature by integrating technological, organizational, and community dimensions into a unified analytical framework. It conceptualizes digital service optimization as an interaction among infrastructure reliability, data interoperability, institutional capacity, and citizens’ digital capabilities, offering a foundation for future research and policy development. The framework also emphasizes that inclusion depends on responsive administration alongside accessible digital systems.

title: OPTIMAL ECONOMIC DISPATCH OF THERMAL POWER GENERATION CONSIDERING LOSSES USING PARTICLE SWARM OPTIMIZATION (PSO)
abstractText: To set the daily schedule for thermal units under rising industrial loads in Vietnam, we calculate the economic dispatch (ED) on a 26-bus grid using a modified version of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Active power losses are calculated from the B-coefficients of Kron. Instead of scattering initial particles at random across the operating limits, we only modify the starting equation to weight each position by the fuel cost of that unit at half capacity. Early iterations are reduced because the swarm starts near cheaper units. On the 26-bus test grid, we reduce the total fuel cost to $15,689.411per hour, which is lower than the costs from random PSO and from the method of Lagrange multipliers. Transmission losses across the network are cut to 26.091 MW.

title: Protonation Isomers in Mass Spectrometry: Ionization, Ion Chemistry, and Interconversion
abstractText: Abstract Protonation isomers (protomers) are structural isomers that differ in the location site of a proton (H+). In mass spectrometry, an understanding of the fundamentals of analyte protonation is essential as the site of protonation influences many gas-phase ion properties, including ion stability, ion fragmentation yields and products, ion–molecule reactivity, photochemistry, conformation, and chirality. If ignored, the presence of protomers can confound the detection and assignment of analyte ions and can also reduce peak loading under many mass spectrometry workflows. In this perspective, we outline how small-molecule protomers arise and discuss the competing mechanisms that govern their relative populations, this implicates electrospray droplet desolvation, ion source reactions, proton-bound dimer stability, ion–molecule reactions, collision-induced internal proton transfer, and photoinduced internal proton transfer. Key concepts are summarized and frontiers for charge-site management are proposed, including deprotonation isomers, metal cations, and multiply charged species.

From Enzyme to Parasite: Enzymatic and Phenotypic-Guided Evaluation of Repurposed Inhibitors against Schistosoma mansoni cathepsin D1 ( Sm CD1)
abstractText: Abstract Schistosomiasis remains a major public health concern in endemic regions, with treatment relying almost exclusively on praziquantel (PZQ). Although vital, PZQ shows limited activity against immature parasites and raises potential resistance concerns. In this context, Schistosoma mansoni cathepsin D1 (SmCD1), an essential enzyme for hemoglobin digestion and parasite development, has emerged as a promising target for the development of new antischistosomal drugs. In this work, we evaluated SmCD1 inhibition by a series of 76 acylguanidine compounds, obtained through a drug repositioning approach. Effects on adult and juvenile worms’ motility and morphology were evaluated by an image-based ex vivo assay, while selected compounds were also tested for cytotoxicity and cell permeability. Upon screening at 10 μM, 11 compounds inhibited at least 90% of SmCD1 activity and/or reduced parasite motility by more than 60% (72h). Three compounds, M3336, M2110, and M8214, potently inhibited SmCD1 (IC50 30–90 nM) with up to 12-fold selectivity for SmCD1 over the human orthologue. Computational analyses identified structural features likely related to potency and selectivity.

Assessing the robustness of machine learning-based automated valuation models across heterogeneous residential markets in Malaysia
abstractText: Purpose This study aims to examine the comparative robustness of machine-learning-based automated valuation models (AVMs) for residential property valuation across different Malaysian market settings. It evaluates random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) and artificial neural network (ANN) models by considering predictive accuracy, temporal consistency and computational feasibility, while distinguishing comparative performance across independently modelled data sets from genuine cross-market transferability. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative comparative approach is applied using an empirical residential property data set from Johor Bahru and simulated scenarios representing Kuala Lumpur and Penang in Malaysia. RF, XGBoost and ANN models are independently developed and evaluated within each case using prediction-error measures and reported temporal performance. Computational execution is assessed separately as an indicator of technical feasibility. The analytical framework interprets model performance as conditional on the interaction between algorithm characteristics, data set structure, preprocessing and validation design rather than as an inherent property of a particular modelling technique. Findings The findings show that relative model performance varies across the evaluated data sets, with different machine-learning approaches demonstrating stronger predictive performance under different conditions. This indicates that there is no universal model that can be assumed to perform consistently across heterogeneous residential market settings. Predictive accuracy and temporal consistency also represent distinct dimensions of model performance, while computational feasibility alone does not establish operational efficiency within professional valuation practice. The findings therefore support context-specific model evaluation, independent validation and continued professional oversight before AVMs are adopted for operational valuation, lending, portfolio management, taxation or mass appraisal applications. Originality/value This study contributes an exploratory framework for evaluating AVMs beyond a simple comparison of predictive accuracy by integrating accuracy, temporal consistency, computational feasibility and the evidential status of the underlying data sets. It further clarifies the distinction between cross-market comparative robustness and model transferability, while positioning AVMs as components of a broader valuation system involving data governance, validation, professional judgement, transparency and accountability. For Malaysia and the wider valuation profession, this study provides a basis for developing more rigorous validation practices, professional guidance and governance frameworks for the responsible integration of machine learning into property valuation.

abstractText: This study evaluated the effects of processing parameters—including slice thickness, citric acid concentration, steaming time, drying temperature, and duration—on the resistant starch content and moisture content of purple yam (Dioscorea alata) flour. The suitable conditions for achieving the highest resistant starch (RS) content (24.28%) were identified as follows: 6 mm slice thickness, soaking in 0.5% citric acid for 30 minutes, steaming for 15 minutes, and drying at 70 °C for 5 hours. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) analysis revealed that the treated starch exhibited a more compact network structure with characteristic swollen regions, indicating physical modification. X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns confirmed a type-C crystalline structure in both control and treated samples. However, the crystallinity index decreased from 46.7% to 40% after treatment, suggesting an increase in the amorphous regions due to thermal processing—an important factor in promoting the formation of RS type III. When applied to bread making, the incorporation of 10% purple yam flour was considered appropriate, improving crumb softness and color while enhancing nutritional value, without compromising the product’s texture compared to the control sample.

Media Pembelajaran Guru Kreatif di Era Transformasi Digital pada Sekolah Menengah Kejuruan Negeri Kabupaten Pasuruan
abstractText: Digital transformation in the world of education requires teachers to be able to adapt to technological developments while developing learning that is creative, innovative, and in accordance with the needs of students. This community service activity aims to improve teachers' competence in utilizing digital technology as a medium and learning resource and encourage the creation of more interactive and student-centered learning. Activities are carried out through socialization, training, direct practice, discussion, and mentoring. Activity materials include the use of digital platforms and applications for learning, the development of interactive learning media, the wise use of artificial intelligence (AI), and strategies for designing digital-based creative learning activities. The results of the activity show an increase in teachers' understanding and skills in selecting, using, and developing digital technology to support the learning process. Teachers are also able to produce more interesting, interactive, and contextual media designs and learning activities. This activity shows that digital transformation is not only related to mastery of technology, but also to teachers' ability to integrate technology, pedagogy, and creativity to create meaningful learning experiences. Thus, strengthening teachers' digital competencies needs to be carried out in a sustainable manner so that teachers are able to become creative, adaptive, and innovative educators in facing educational changes in the digital era.

title: Evaluation of stream habitat suitability using the HMUs clustering method and habitat diversity index
abstractText: Abstract The objectives of this study were to classify streamflow patterns into Hydro-Morphological Units (HMUs) using hydrodynamic factors and to evaluate stream habitats based on these HMU clusters. A 2.9 km reach of the Bokha stream was selected as the study area, where aquatic habitat enhancement is required. Stream velocity and water depth were simulated using the HEC-RAS 2D model. Based on the simulation results, the stream flow patterns were categorized into five HMU types—pools, riffles, rapids, ruffles, and runs—according to estimated probabilities derived from their respective hydrodynamic boundary ranges. Spatiotemporal analysis indicated that HMUs such as ruffle and run closely corresponded with observed fish habitat characteristics, suggesting their suitability as indicators for habitat evaluation. To quantitatively assess habitat diversity, the Normalized Shannon–Weaver Index was calculated, yielding values of 0.93 at the minimum ecological streamflow (0.48 m³/s) and 0.88 at the maximum Weighted Usable Area (WUA) flow (6.9 m³/s). Overall, the proposed approach provides a robust framework for stream habitat evaluation and contributes to the identification of streamflow ranges that are both ecologically meaningful and practically feasible, thereby supporting sustainable stream management strategies.

title: An Exploratory Comparison of Local Thermal Responses in Compacted and Uncompacted Magnesium Alloy Chip-Bed Fires
abstractText: Magnesium alloy chip-bed fires may exhibit different local thermal behaviors depending on the packing conditions. This study compared fires under uncompacted and compacted conditions by evaluating the local temperature, heat flux, and visible flame behavior. The results indicated that the uncompacted bed exhibited high-temperature responses over a broader region, whereas the compacted bed exhibited more localized responses at higher temperatures. Variations were also observed in the spatial distribution, arrival times of the high-temperature responses, and in the temperature-heat flux relationship. These findings indicate that the effect of compaction should be evaluated based on the spatial extent, localization, and temporal characteristics of the local thermal responses, rather than the maximum temperature alone.

title: Explainable AI Analysis of Future Domestic Water Shortages in Local Water Supply Systems: A Case Study of the Seomjin River Basin
abstractText: This study applied an integrated K-WEAP and XGBoost-SHAP framework to identify the characteristics of domestic water shortages and their key explanatory factors under climate change conditions in the Seomjin River water system. Three representative drought scenarios with high drought vulnerability were selected from CMIP6 climate projections, and domestic water shortage rates were simulated for 11 administrative districts using K-WEAP. XGBoost surrogate models developed for four districts with sufficient shortage samples achieved coefficients of determination exceeding 0.91 on the test dataset. SHAP analysis identified regional and local water supplies, reservoir supply, and direct river intake as the primary explanatory factors, although their relative importance varied across districts. In general, decreases in major water supply variables were associated with increases in predicted shortage rates, suggesting that the dominant drivers of domestic water shortages differ depending on the composition of local water sources and the structure of the water supply system.

title: Asymptotic Solution to the Fsair Epidemic Model and Unique Identification of the Fractional Order
abstractText: This article deals with the asymptotic solution to the fractional-order SAIR (FSAIR) epidemic model and identification of the order of the fractional derivative by using an observation of the recovered group at a given time. A unique solution to the forward problem is proved to be global and nonnegative under suitable conditions on the model parameters. The asymptotic solution is derived by the Laplace-Adomian decomposition method (L-ADM) and is shown to converge to the exact solution of the forward problem through an analysis of the Gamma function and Adomian polynomials. Furthermore, the computability of the asymptotic solution is illustrated by numerical analysis, through which the inverse order problem is transformed into an algebraic equation, and uniqueness of the inverse problem is obtained from the monotonicity of the nonlinear function of the order.

title: A Study on Information Requirements for Evacuees in Augmented Reality (AR)-Based Evacuation Route Guidance During Flood Disasters
abstractText: This study presents a mixed-methods framework that integrates latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA)-based topic modeling and content analysis to identify the information requirements for augmented reality (AR)-assisted evacuation guidance systems during flood disasters. A corpus of academic papers and operations manuals related to disaster evacuation was compiled and processed using a seven-stage preprocessing pipeline, and an LDA model was constructed to extract latent topics. The extracted topics were assigned to five theoretically grounded categories with confirmed inter-rater reliability (Cohen's κ = 0.72), and the category distributions between the two source types were explored through a comparative analysis. The route and shelter location information, AR interface and information delivery mechanisms, behavioral decision support information, and hazardous environment information were identified as the core information requirements for AR evacuation guidance systems. In conclusion, these findings provide an empirical foundation for the information design of AR-based evacuation systems and highlight the research–practice gap that must be bridged to provide effective real-time guidance for evacuees in flood disaster scenarios.

title: HIGHER-ORDER POLE SOLUTIONS OF THE (2+1) DIMENSIONAL CDGKSEQUATION
abstractText: Abstract The present study is devoted to the systematic construction of a novel class of N- multipole solutions for the (2+1) dimensional Caudrey–Dodd–Gibbon–Kotera–Sawada (CDGKS) e- quation. Within the inverse scattering transform formalism, we address the technically demanding regime where the underlying transmission coefficient exhibits multiple pairs of higher-order singulari- ties. The formulation of the inverse problem as a 2×2 matrix Riemann-Hilbert problem, supplemented by discrete residue constraints, reveals that potential reconstruction in the reflectionless case collapses into a closed-form linear algebraic system. Drawing upon the algebraic properties of generalized con- fluent Cauchy matrices, Gram matrices, and Jordan-associated polynomial functions, we rigorously establish the well-posedness of the solution for all (x,y,t) ∈ R2× R+. This foundation allows for the derivation of compatible higher-order pole solutions within the mKdV and fifth-order mKdV equation- s. Subsequently, explicit multipole solutions for the (2+1) dimensional CDGKS equation are obtained by invoking integrable decomposition and modular square transformations. Numerical visualizations further elucidate the dynamical evolution and density profiles of these localized waves, revealing the intricate interaction patterns of higher-order, bound-state solitons and breathers.
