Substrate-Controlled Divergent Oxidative Cross-Coupling Reaction via Dual-Chelation-Assisted Strategy: −SMe/–SeMe as Traceless Directing Groups
abstractText: Abstract A dual-chelation-assisted oxidative C8–H/C2–H cross-coupling between 1-chalcogen-substituted naphthalenes and benzamides under the Rh/Ag/HFIP catalytic system is disclosed herein, which features excellent regio- and chemoselectivity. When thiomethyl (−SMe) serves as the directing group, only 2-methoxy-substituted thioethers undergo in situ removal of this directing group, whereas other substrates are resistant to C–S bond cleavage. Replacing thiomethyl with selenomethyl (−SeMe) results in smooth C–Se bond cleavage for all selenoether substrates. This strategy enables a substrate-controlled divergent synthesis of biaryls, and represents the first example of utilizing −SMe and −SeMe as traceless directing groups.

title: Spatiotemporal Consistency Analysis of KMA, JMA, and JTWC Tropical Cyclone Track Records: Inter-Agency Comparison
abstractText: The western North Pacific is one of the most active regions for tropical cyclone activity worldwide, and the reliability of long-term typhoon best-track data is critical for assessing storm surges and marine disasters along the Korean Peninsula. This study quantitatively analyzed the inter-agency consistency of the center position, central pressure, and maximum sustained wind speed among the KMA, JMA, and JTWC best-track datasets for 1977-2024. Identical tropical cyclones were matched using IBTrACS storm identifiers, and records from the same observation times were compared. This is an inter-agency consistency analysis, not an accuracy validation against independent observations. The results revealed a three-stage characteristic in the KMA-JMA comparison: the records were nearly identical at the reported coordinate resolution during 1977-2000, showed some discrepancies during 2001-2013, and diverged distinctly after 2014, following the introduction of the KMA’s independent reanalysis system. Although positional differences were generally small, distinct discrepancies appeared in specific periods and intensity-related variables, depending on agency-specific listing criteria, analysis systems, and reporting practices. In particular, the comparison of maximum sustained wind speed between JMA and JTWC showed that the difference between the 10-minute and 1-minute averaging periods was the primary structural factor, and the JMA/JTWC wind-speed ratio varied from 1.34 to 0.79 depending on tropical cyclone intensity. The inter-agency wind-speed ratio was close to the conventional conversion factor of 0.88 in the Cat. 1 range, but deviated systematically from 0.88 in the tropical depression and strong typhoon ranges, indicating that a constant conversion factor applied across all intensity ranges can introduce intensity-dependent bias. These results indicate that the choice of the best-track dataset and wind speed conversion method is a major source of uncertainty in storm surge modeling and tropical cyclone climate analysis around the Korean Peninsula and that agency datasets should be selected according to the analysis purpose.

title: Determination of the Muzzle-to-Target Distance in Shooting Cases Using Inductively Coupled Plasma – Optical Emission Analysis of Barium, Lead, and Antimony
abstractText: Between 2015 and 2023 firearm-related deaths almost doubled in the U.S., increasing discussions concerning gun control measurements. Gun regulations vary between states. States like Mississippi have not only relaxed gun control laws but also the highest firearm-related deaths. Research involving inorganic gunshot residue (IGSR) typically focuses on the shooter end rather than the target material. This work aimed to create a mathematical relationship between the concentration of metals on target materials and the muzzle-to-target distance for the estimation of shooting distance. Cloth samples containing IGSRs were obtained by shooting a Remington UMC 9mm Luger ammunition from a Smith & Wesson M&P9 Shield semi-automatic pistol in a controlled indoor environment at varying distances. The IGSR was extracted from samples using an acid digestion procedure and analyzed using Inductively Coupled Plasma-Optical Emission Spectroscopy (ICP-OES) to quantify barium, lead, and antimony. A mathematical model was developed for the interpretation of barium, lead, and antimony in both ammunitions analyzed. Polynomial regression was employed as an exploratory tool to visualize the non-linear relationship between IGSR concentration and shooting distance within the experimental range studied. This research provides evidence that the relationship between muzzle-to-target distance and the concentration of metal on the target material not only exists but is polynomial. The results demonstrate a measurable non-linear relationship between inorganic gunshot residue deposition and shooting distance. While additional validation across different firearms, ammunition types, and target materials is required, these findings provide evidence supporting the future development of quantitative approaches for shooting distance estimation.

Model Internalisasi Nilai Ekoteologi melalui Dakwah Bil-Hal dalam Program Kokurikuler Sekolah di SD Al-Ishlah Tulungagung
abstractText: This study aims to analyze the model of ecotheological value internalization through bil-hal da’wah in school co-curricular programs at SD Al-Ishlah Tulungagung. The research employed a qualitative approach with a field research design to examine how ecotheological values are introduced, practiced, and integrated into students’ daily habits. Data were collected through observation, interviews, and documentation focusing on the implementation of the Urban Farming program. The findings reveal that ecotheological values are internalized through practical environmental activities, including plant cultivation, environmental care habits, and religious reflections connecting environmental preservation with human responsibility as Khalifah fil Ardh. These activities provide opportunities for students to relate religious values to concrete actions in caring for their surroundings. The internalization model consists of four interconnected components: value transformation, value transaction, value transinternalization, and ecological-spiritual habituation. Its implementation positively contributes to students’ environmental awareness, responsibility, patience, compassion, and spiritual consciousness. This study concludes that bil-hal da’wah through environmental co-curricular activities effectively promotes ecotheological education and character development by integrating practical environmental engagement with religious understanding among elementary school students.

title: Mean Sea-Level Pressure Patterns during Springtime Strong Winds in Gangneung: Consistency with Principal Component Modes over the Korean Peninsula
abstractText: Springtime strong winds on the east side of the Taebaek Mountains in Korea constitute a critical meteorological hazard that not only causes direct damage but also triggers serious secondary disasters such as rapid spread of wildfires, threats to aviation safety, and dispersion of atmospheric pollutants. To examine this phenomenon, principal component analysis (PCA) was applied to spring daily mean sea-level pressure (MSLP) fields (2016-2025). Wind-speed cases were classified using the ASOS data for Gangneung. PC1-PC3 explained 86.3% of the total variance (PC1 alone explained 62.1% of the total variance), capturing most of the MSLP variability. For strong-wind cases, the spatial correlation between the original and reconstructed MSLP fields increased from about 0.7 with PC1 to 0.87 with PC1-PC3. These results demonstrated high consistency: springtime strong winds in Gangneung are driven by a distinct south-high and north-low MSLP pattern that closely matches the overarching principal modes over the Korean Peninsula. Consequently, the effective utilization of these springtime synoptic MSLP patterns is key to improving the prediction of strong wind occurrences in Gangneung, thereby providing essential insights for proactive disaster mitigation.

title: Multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging histogram and habitat analysis for predicting 1p/19q codeletion in isocitrate dehydrogenase-mutant gliomas
abstractText: Abstract Background Quantitative T2-FLAIR analysis and multiparametric MRI habitat imaging may provide noninvasive information regarding 1p/19q status in IDH-mutant gliomas. The primary aim was to determine whether adding habitat-derived features to whole-region histogram features improves prediction of 1p/19q codeletion. We retrospectively analyzed 122 patients with World Health Organization grade 2 or 3 gliomas. Precontrast T1-weighted, postcontrast T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and FLAIR images were normalized using patient-specific normal-appearing white matter. Whole-region histogram, habitat-derived, and combined models were evaluated in whole-tumor and tumor-core-like regions using 20 repetitions of nested fivefold cross-validation. Results In the whole-tumor analysis, the whole-region histogram, habitat-derived, and combined models achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.747, 0.681, and 0.734, respectively. The corresponding values in the tumor-core-like analysis were 0.777, 0.734, and 0.766. The whole-tumor habitat-derived model had a lower area under the curve than the whole-region histogram model, with a difference of − 0.066 (95% confidence interval, − 0.130 to − 0.003). The combined model did not improve discrimination in either region. Whole-tumor habitat centroids were more stable than tumor-core-like centroids. Conclusions Whole-region histogram features provided moderate discrimination of 1p/19q codeletion, whereas habitat-derived features did not provide incremental predictive value. T2-FLAIR difference and T2-weighted distributional features were selected most consistently. These findings support further evaluation of the simpler histogram approach in independent datasets but do not support replacement of tissue-based molecular testing.

title: Association of antibiotic exposure with Kawasaki disease
abstractText: Abstract Kawasaki disease (KD) is an acute febrile vasculitis of unknown etiology that primarily affects children under five years old. Emerging evidence suggests that gut microbiota alterations may contribute to KD pathogenesis. Because antibiotics modify intestinal microbial composition, their inappropriate or repeated use in early childhood may increase KD susceptibility. However, population-based evidence linking antibiotic exposure with KD onset remains limited, and the influence of antibiotic class, number of antibiotic prescriptions, and administration route has not been systematically evaluated. To examine the association between antibiotic type, number of antibiotic prescriptions, route of administration, and KD onset in a nationwide dataset. We conducted a matched case–control study using the JMDC database (2005–2024). Children aged 0–6 years were eligible. Newly diagnosed KD cases ( n = 17,410) and controls ( n = 68,621) were matched 1:4 by age, sex, and birth year. Antibiotic exposure from birth until one month before the index date was assessed by class (penicillins, cephalosporins, macrolides, quinolones, others), number of antibiotic prescriptions, and administration route (oral vs. intravenous). Multivariable conditional logistic regression estimated odds of KD onset adjusted for antiviral agent use, antifungal agent use, preterm birth, and low birth weight, with matching by age, sex, and birth year accounted for in the conditional analysis. Among 86,031 children, exposure to penicillins (OR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.21–1.34), cephalosporins (OR, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.10–1.23), quinolones (OR, 1.48; 95% CI, 1.27–1.73), and macrolides (OR, 1.19; 95% CI, 1.09–1.31) was associated with increased KD risk. Higher odds of KD were observed with increasing numbers of antibiotic prescriptions (≥ 5 prescriptions: OR, 1.22; 95% CI, 1.16–1.28). Oral antibiotic use showed a significant association (OR, 1.22; 95% CI, 1.16–1.27), while intravenous use did not. Repeated antibiotic prescriptions, especially via oral administration, were associated with KD. These findings support an association between prior antibiotic exposure and KD, warranting further mechanistic investigation.

title: The Effect of Work-Life Balance on Employee Performance in Cirebon City’s General Affairs Division
abstractText: This study investigates how work-life balance affects employee performance in the general affairs unit of the Cirebon City Regional Secretariat. A quantitative, descriptive-associative design was used, with a five-point Likert questionnaire completed by all 53 employees of the unit (saturated sampling). Work-life balance was analyzed both as a single construct and through its three dimensions (time, involvement, and satisfaction balance), with age, tenure, education, and gender as controls. The analysis covered validity, reliability, and Average Variance Extracted (AVE), classical assumption tests, simple and multiple regression, and a two-stage least squares check using Wu-Hausman and Sargan tests. Work-life balance was rated good (mean = 4.01) and performance very good (mean = 4.39). Work-life balance affected performance positively (Y = 40.918 + 0.366X, t = 2.740, p = 0.008, R² = 0.128), although the effect was weaker with heteroscedasticity-robust errors (p = 0.061). Of the dimensions, only involvement balance was significant (B = 0.943, p = 0.006). The findings suggest that work-life balance is positively associated with employee performance, particularly through involvement balance, although the relationship becomes less statistically robust after adjusting for heteroscedasticity. Endogeneity was not detected (Wu-Hausman p = 0.294), but the instruments were weak and the work-life balance scale showed modest reliability (α = 0.549). The results apply to one administrative unit and should be interpreted cautiously. This study contributes empirical evidence on the dimensional effects of work-life balance in local government administration and highlights employee involvement balance as a potential priority for improving performance management practices.

title: Comparison of Serum Creatinine Levels in Controlled and Uncontrolled Diabetes Mellitus Patients Based on HbA1c Levels at Hermina Arcamanik Hospital
abstractText: Diabetes mellitus can lead to renal complications as a consequence of poor glycemic control. HbA1c is used to assess glycemic control, whereas serum creatinine can assist in evaluating kidney function. This study aimed to determine differences in serum creatinine levels between patients with controlled and uncontrolled diabetes mellitus based on HbA1c levels at Hermina Arcamanik General Hospital, Bandung. A quantitative comparative design with a cross-sectional approach was employed. Data were obtained from the medical records of patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus, involving 100 samples from a population of 150 patients. Analysis was performed using the Shapiro–Wilk test and the Paired Samples t-test. The mean serum creatinine level was 0.681 mg/dL in the controlled group and 1.02 mg/dL in the uncontrolled group. The data were normally distributed, with p-values of 0.168 and 0.459, respectively. The Paired Samples t-test demonstrated a statistically significant difference (p<0.001), with a mean difference of 0.339 mg/dL. Thus, serum creatinine levels differed significantly between controlled and uncontrolled diabetes mellitus patients, with the uncontrolled group showing a higher mean value. Assessment of kidney function should also consider additional parameters, particularly estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR).

title: School principals’ perceptions of generative AI as a decision-support tool: implications for decisional capital
abstractText: Purpose This study examines how generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is perceived as a decision-support mechanism in school principals’ decision-making, focusing on its perceived implications for decisional capital within a centralized education system. Design/methodology/approach Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 17 public school principals across different school levels in Türkiye. Data were analyzed using thematic analysis to identify how GenAI is interpreted and positioned within principals’ decision-making processes. Findings Principals reported decision-making challenges driven by bureaucratic procedures, restricted autonomy and competing stakeholder demands. Within these constraints, GenAI was seen not as a substitute for professional judgment but as cognitive support that may improve access to information, facilitate scenario-based reasoning and inform evidence-based judgments. Principals reported varying levels of readiness to integrate GenAI into organizational decision-making, with this variation associated with digital competence, institutional support and ethical awareness. Originality/value The study extends discussions of principals’ decision-making by linking GenAI-enabled decision support to the exercise of decisional capital under centralized governance constraints, highlighting conditions under which GenAI may contribute to human-centered and ethically grounded organizational decision-making processes.

title: Optimization of phase-contrast MRI shunt flow measurement across multiple scanners for the management of hydrocephalus
abstractText: OBJECTIVE Ventricular shunts divert CSF in patients with hydrocephalus, often providing lifesaving intervention. Untreated shunt failure can lead to increased intracranial pressure and subsequent neurological injury. Phase-contrast MRI (PC-MRI) is a noninvasive technique to assess shunt function by measuring shunt flow. This work assists in clinical implementation of PC-MRI by quantifying and accounting for sources of variation in shunt flow measurements. METHODS Shunt phantoms were used to provide consistency between scanners, with flow rates spanning a physiological range. Ten MRI scanner/coil combinations with variable field strength (0.55–7T), manufacturer (Siemens and Philips), coil design (8-, 16-, 20-, and 32-channel), gradient strength (22, 33, 40, 80, and 200 mT/m), and gradient slew rate (55, 125, 160, 200, and 1000 T/m/sec) were tested. Sequence parameters were optimized for each scanner, and flow rates were extracted using three analytical methods that calculate flow: 1) mean fluid velocity, 2) maximum fluid velocity, and 3) a parabolic model of laminar flow. PC-MRI measurements were plotted against known flow rates to compare accuracy and precision across scanners. A phantom incorporating four commonly used catheter models was designed to assess variability introduced by catheter-related magnetic susceptibility artifact. RESULTS The authors show that PC-MRI can be successfully performed across a wide range of MRI scanners, including the first measurements of shunt flow at low (0.55T) and high (7T) magnetic field strength. The comparison dataset between scanners from the single-catheter phantom included 400 independent acquisitions and 1600 unique postprocessed flow values. The highest accuracy was achieved using a parabolic fit of the shunt flow profile combined with background phase correction. Advanced modeling reduced the mean absolute error ± standard deviation between measured and true flow rates from 2.0 ± 2.4 to 0.88 ± 1.1 mL/hr. These resulting deviations were at the observed range of physiological variation, even on low-field scanners. The authors performed additional scans to quantify manageable sources of variability, including shim placement, image plane angle, and human analytical error. Differences between catheter models did not significantly affect measured flow values. CONCLUSIONS PC-MRI enables accurate shunt flow measurement across diverse MRI platforms (10 scanner/coil combinations tested and all found to function), including at field strengths of 0.55T and 7T. Standardized protocols reduce error and will help support expanded use of the technique.

title: Comparison of rocuronium‑sugammadex and mivacurium on recovery efficiency after pediatric isolated adenoidectomy: a propensity score‑matched cohort study
abstractText: Abstract Background Mivacurium and rocuronium-sugammadex are two commonly used neuromuscular blocking regimens in pediatric otorhinolaryngological surgery. However, existing comparative studies frequently combine isolated adenoidectomy with adenotonsillectomy, introducing significant confounding variables; consequently, dedicated head-to-head comparisons restricted to isolated adenoidectomy remain scarce. This study aimed to compare postoperative recovery efficiency between rocuronium-sugammadex reversal and mivacurium monotherapy, two routinely used clinical regimens, in children aged 3–12 years undergoing isolated adenoidectomy. Methods Of 877 eligible children, 616 children (308 matched pairs) were analyzed after 1:1 propensity-score matching. The primary endpoint was the time from cessation of anesthetic maintenance agents to tracheal extubation. Secondary endpoints included time from anesthetic cessation to post-anaesthesia care unit (PACU) discharge, emergence quality, and postoperative pain scores. Results The median time from anesthetic discontinuation to extubation was 23 min in the rocuronium-sugammadex group versus 25 min in the mivacurium group Hodges-Lehmann (HL) pseudomedian difference − 2 min; (95% CI − 4.00 to − 0.0001; P = 0.022). However, this modest between-group difference was not statistically significant in a paired sensitivity analysis ( P = 0.069). The median interval from drug cessation to PACU discharge was shorter in the rocuronium-sugammadex group (38 [30.00–48.00] min) than in the mivacurium group (42 [34.00–51.00] min), with a HL pseudomedian difference of − 4.00 min (95% CI − 6.00 to − 2.00; P < 0.001). Steward scores were comparable ( P = 0.416); VAS pain scores differed statistically ( P = 0.016) but the absolute difference was minimal. Subgroup analysis showed that shorter extubation time was observed only in children receiving intraoperative midazolam. Shorter PACU discharge duration was also seen in this subgroup and in both age subgroups, but not in children without midazolam. Conclusion In children undergoing isolated adenoidectomy, the rocuronium-sugammadex regimen was associated with modestly shorter extubation time in primary analysis, though this finding was not confirmed in paired sensitivity analysis, together with significantly reduced PACU discharge time and delayed discharge risk, without compromising postoperative recovery safety or comfort. Benefits in extubation time and PACU discharge duration were observed primarily in children receiving intraoperative midazolam; however, formal interaction analysis for this exploratory subgroup comparison did not demonstrate significant effect modification. Taken together, under real-world clinical dosing conditions, these findings suggest that this rocuronium-sugammadex anesthetic strategy may help optimize patient turnover in high-volume pediatric day-surgery centers.

title: Water Quality Changes along the South Platte River in the Denver Metro Area: PFAS, Organic, and Select Inorganic Constituents
abstractText: Abstract The South Platte River is a major Colorado waterway and effluent-dominated river receiving inputs from wastewater treatment plants and tributaries. Among the contaminants of concern, poly- and perfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) have gained increasing attention due to their persistence and widespread occurrence in impacted rivers. This study investigates the occurrence, composition, and spatial variability of PFAS and select constituents in the South Platte River. Samples were collected (two campaigns) from multiple locations along the river (upstream, downstream, side streams, and major wastewater discharge points) and analyzed for both regulated and unregulated PFAS, major ions, nitrogen species, total organic carbon, and sucralose. Results indicate that effluents from wastewater treatment facilities are important contributors to nutrient loading and the primary source of sucralose in the river. However, total detected PFAS concentrations in several natural tributaries exceeded those in all effluents, highlighting the substantial role of tributary inputs in watershed PFAS loading and variability. Moreover, river foam samples contained PFAS concentrations of ∼25,000 ng/L, substantially higher than surrounding waters, highlighting the potential for foam-mediated contaminant transport. Results indicate that while sucralose effectively traces municipal wastewater inputs, its lack of correlation with total detected PFAS concentrations limits its use as a standalone tool for PFAS source attribution in complex watersheds.

title: The Cumulative Distribution Function-Based Method for Random Drift Model
abstractText: We propose a numerical method to uniformly handle the random genetic drift model for pure drift, natural selection and mutation. For pure drift and natural selection cases, the Dirac \(\delta\) singularity will develop at two boundary ends and the mass lumped at the two ends stands for the fixation probability. For the one-way mutation case, known as Muller’s ratchet, the accumulation of deleterious mutations leads to the loss of the fittest gene; the Dirac \(\delta\) singularity will spike only at one boundary end, which stands for the fixation of the deleterious gene and loss of the fittest one. For the two-way mutation case, the singularity with negative power law may emerge near boundary points. We first rewrite the original model on the probability density function (PDF) to one with respect to the cumulative distribution function (CDF). Dirac \(\delta\) singularity of the PDF becomes the discontinuity of the CDF. Then we establish a revised finite difference method (rFDM), which can keep the total probability, is positivity-preserving and is unconditionally stable. The advantage of our algorithm is that it is straightforward and preserves the moment for pure drift and natural selection. For all cases involved, it can be proven that after a long time, the numerical solution converges to the numerical steady state. This is another advantage, and it means that the numerical scheme can catch the discontinuous jump of the CDF, and accurately predict the fixation probability for pure drift, natural selection and one-way mutation. Meanwhile, for the two-way mutation case, it can also catch the power law of the singularity accurately. The numerical results show the effectiveness of the scheme. Finally, by comparing rFDM with a standard finite difference method (sFDM), we find that for the pure drift problem, sFDM fails to keep the conservation of expectation and cannot predict the fixation probability accurately, because an artificial mutation is introduced near two boundary ends. For the two-way mutation case, sFDM fails to predict the correct power law of the singularity.

title: Midwifery Care For Pregnant Women Obesity And Hypertension : A Case Study
abstractText: Obesity during pregnancy is defined as excessive weight gain exceeding 12–16 kg above the normal range. This condition can trigger metabolic and cardiovascular complications, including hyperglycemia, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. Gestational hypertension is characterized by an increase in blood pressure to 140/90 mmHg or higher after 20 weeks of gestation. Such conditions elevate the risk of complications and may potentially lead to mortality for both the mother and the infant. Objective: This study aims to examine the influence of obesity on hypertension in pregnant women and to identify preventive measures to reduce the risk of both conditions during pregnancy. Methods: A case study design was employed, focusing on a 36 year old pregnant woman (G2P1001) at 33–34 weeks of gestation with a single, viable intrauterine pregnancy, complicated by obesity and hypertension. Data were collected through interviews, physical examinations, observations, and documentation. The diagnosis was based on body mass index (BMI) assessment and blood pressure measurements. Interventions included pregnancy monitoring, nutritional counseling for a balanced diet, weight gain management, and health education. Results: The findings indicate a strong association between obesity and hypertension in pregnant women. Conclusion: Obesity influences the occurrence of hypertension in pregnant women

Affine-Invariant Trigonometric WENO Finite Difference Schemes for Hyperbolic Conservation Laws
abstractText: Novel affine-invariant trigonometric weighted essentially non-oscillatory (Ai-TWENO) finite difference schemes are proposed to improve the accuracy and robustness of existing TWENO schemes in capturing small-scale discontinuities and highly oscillatory solutions. By systematically developing a fifth-order WENO operator based on trigonometric polynomials, a comprehensive mathematical framework is presented that can be generalized to higher-order schemes. The existence of cell-size dependency of the non-polynomial-based WENO operator is analyzed. A three-step Ai-weighting process–de-averaging, de-scaling, and re-averaging–is introduced to ensure the affine-invariant property for both polynomial and non-polynomial basis functions and the essential non-oscillatory property. Numerical experiments on Euler equations demonstrate the improved performance of Ai-TWENO schemes in resolving small-scale structures and maintaining robustness in the presence of shocks and contact discontinuities. Moreover, the Ai-TWENO schemes for steady-state shallow water equations confirm the effectiveness of achieving a well-balanced property. These findings suggest that the proposed framework is a promising tool for developing high-order shock-capturing schemes with broad applicability in complex flow structures.

Artificial intelligence in offshore wind geotechnical engineering: A lifecycle-oriented review
abstractText: Abstract As offshore wind develops toward deeper waters and larger turbine capacities, geotechnical challenges are becoming increasingly complex, involving more variable seabed conditions, larger foundation dimensions, and stricter lifecycle reliability and cost-control requirements. Accordingly, artificial intelligence (AI), with strengths in data fusion, surrogate modeling, and monitoring-informed inference, has increasingly been explored as a complementary computational and analytical tool in offshore wind geotechnical engineering. Particular attention is given to spatially variable ground characterization, surrogate-based response and reliability assessment, and monitoring-informed evaluation of installation and service states. This paper presents a lifecycle-oriented review of AI applications, informed by systematically screened research articles published between 2001 and 2025 and selected project- and industry-level practices. The main AI application pathways are synthesized across site investigation, foundation design, installation, and operation and maintenance (O&M), and are related to stage-specific geotechnical problems rather than algorithm categories alone. The synthesis shows a differentiated maturity pattern across the lifecycle. Foundation design shows the highest research concentration, while project-level digital ground modeling in site investigation and design-stage surrogate analysis show the clearest pathways to engineering use. Closed-loop installation control and below-mudline state inference for O&M remain largely at the research or validation stage. Across these applications, several cross-cutting limitations remain, including sparse offshore data, insufficient physical constraints, limited cross-site generalizability, incomplete standardization, and limited engineering acceptance. Future directions are discussed, including physics-integrated models, high-quality data ecosystems supported by standardized benchmark datasets, certification-oriented validation, and reviewable agent-assisted workflows to support more reliable and cost-effective offshore wind development.

title: A Study on the Fire Occurrence Characteristics of Personal Lithium Battery Devices
abstractText: According to fire data from the National Fire Data System (NFDS) Big Data Platform, fires involving personal lithium-ion battery devices surged 3.2-fold, from 69 cases in 2019 to 219 in 2025. As lithium batteries are increasingly being adopted in personal devices such as electric kickboards, electric bicycles, and portable chargers, the associated fire risk has increased. However, a comprehensive analysis of fire occurrence characteristics and ignition causes for these devices remains limited. To address this gap, this study analyzed 1,157 personal lithium battery device fires from 2019 to 2025 and examined the occurrence characteristics by device type, location of origin, time of day, ignition cause composition, and casualty characteristics. The results revealed distinct variations in the ignition-cause composition across different device types, indicating that device-specific approaches, rather than uniform prevention measures, are necessary. These findings provide foundational data to establish targeted fire prevention measures and improve safety standards for personal lithium battery devices.

The relationship of autonomy with hybrid worker well-being and productivity - the mediating role of managerial culture
abstractText: Purpose Knowledge work is extensively location-independent, making flexible work designs more common. However, organizations foster various practices regarding the level of autonomy and control, affecting employee well-being and productivity. To support strategic and operative work design, this paper aims to explain the relationship of autonomy with hybrid worker well-being and productivity, considering the mediating role of managerial culture. Design/methodology/approach This paper describes a quantitative survey featuring 1,057 respondents. It tests with a regression analysis a hypothesized model, in which the level of individual work autonomy, mediated by managerial culture, predicts well-being and productivity. Findings The analysis indicated that decision-making autonomy has a direct positive relationship with productivity. Furthermore, autonomy in working practices has a direct positive relationship with both well-being and productivity. Managerial culture mediates the relationship between decision-making autonomy and both outcome variables. Originality/value This paper provides empirical evidence of the relationship of autonomy with hybrid worker well-being and productivity. The academic value of this paper lies in the multiple dimensions of autonomy it addresses, yielding novel data on the outcomes in a comparative manner. As a pragmatic contribution, it provides input to managerial culture design.

title: INTEGRATIVE MULTI‑MARKER BARCODING AND ITS PHYLOGENY RESOLVE VIETNAMESE STRAIN CCAH013/2 AS Mychonastes rotundus (Sphaeropleales, Chlorophyceae)
abstractText: A coccoid green microalga (strain CCAH013/2) isolated from a mangrove edge freshwater site in Can Gio, Viet Nam was identified through an integrative workflow combining morphology with multi marker DNA evidence. Nuclear 18S rRNA and plastid 23S rRNA sequences showed very high similarity to named Mychonastes taxa, supporting placement at the genus level but offering limited interspecific resolution due to locus conservatism. The ITS region (ITS1–5.8S–ITS2) provided species level power: BLAST results reached ≥ 99% identity to Mychonastes rotundus and dropped markedly for other congeners (≤~ 95%). A maximum likelihood tree inferred from ITS recovered CCAH013/2 within the M. rotundus clade with strong bootstrap support, mirroring the pairwise identity pattern. Morphological characters-small, spherical to slightly oval, non motile cells occurring in minute clusters and reproducing by autospores-were congruent with the emended generic concept and the species diagnosis. Together, these data support a robust assignment of CCAH013/2 to Mychonastes rotundus and provide a basis for applied studies under local conditions, including CO₂ enrichment tolerance, lipid and carotenoid productivity, and small scale pilot tests in tropical coastal freshwater niches.

title: Weather extremes and diarrheal disease: findings from a multi-city study in the Asia Pacific Region
abstractText: Abstract Background Changes in weather patterns including increasing extreme weather events tied to ongoing climate change is impacting burden of diarrheal disease, yet there is a paucity of data regarding how this risk varies across large urban areas within the high-risk Asia Pacific Region (APR). We investigated the association between weather extremes (temperature, precipitation) and risk of diarrheal disease burden in large metropolitan areas of APR. Method We obtained diarrheal disease records from 17 cities located across the APR, including cities in Nepal, Taiwan, Vietnam, India, Singapore, and Indonesia. We used a distributed lag non-linear model to investigate the association between exposure to weather extremes (high: 95th percentile and low: 5th percentile of temperature and precipitation) and diarrheal disease burden. City-specific risk estimates were subsequently pooled using multivariate random-effects meta-analysis. Results A total of 10,358,987 diarrheal disease cases were included. Considerable heterogeneity was observed in temperature- and precipitation-related associations across cities. At the pooled level, neither extreme low nor extreme high temperature was significantly associated with diarrheal disease, with RRs of 1.02 (95% CI: 0.88–1.19) and 1.09 (95% CI: 0.96–1.24), respectively; pooled associations with extreme precipitation were also not statistically significant. However, extreme high temperature was associated with increased risk in Ahmedabad (RR: 2.32; 95% CI: 1.43–3.74), while extreme low temperature was associated with increased risk in Kaohsiung (RR: 1.83; 95% CI: 1.39–2.41). Latitude-specific analyses suggested stronger associations with extreme low temperature at higher latitudes and somewhat stronger associations with extreme high temperature at lower latitudes. Conclusion Our data point to significant spatial heterogeneity in diarrheal disease burden associated with exposure to extreme temperatures and precipitation. Public health adaptation strategies designed to help communities adapt to health threats of climate change need to account for such heterogeneity.

title: Food and Drug Administration authorization of spine surgery devices: a 2-decade analysis of clearance trends, regulatory pathways, and market entry
abstractText: OBJECTIVE In this study, the authors aimed to characterize trends in the regulatory authorization of spine surgery devices in the United States, including device category composition, regulatory pathway use, decision timelines, and patterns of new market entry. METHODS Authorizations related to spine surgery issued between January 1, 2000, and December 31, 2023, were identified from the publicly available US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) 510(k), Premarket Approval (PMA), De Novo, and Humanitarian Device Exemption databases and classified into one of 7 categories (spinal implants and fixation, navigation, bone graft and augmentation, surgical instruments, neuromodulation and nerve, measurement and diagnostics, and other) according to intended use. Annual authorization volume, regulatory pathway, decision time, device class, sponsor experience, and manufacturer location were extracted, and category-level trends were evaluated using 3-year trailing averages. Group comparisons were performed using one-way ANOVA and Welch’s t-test. RESULTS A total of 5977 spine devices were authorized over the study period. Spinal implants and fixation accounted for most devices (n = 4328, 72.4%), followed by navigation (n = 753, 12.6%). Annual authorization volume more than doubled from 108 devices in 2000 to 342 in 2023. During the same period, the proportional share represented by spinal implants and fixation declined from 78.7% to 50.9%, while navigation increased from 0% to 31.3%, reaching 107 authorizations by 2023 and emerging as the second-largest spine category. The 510(k) pathway accounted for 99.4% of all authorizations. Special 510(k) submissions cleared faster than traditional submissions (59.1 vs 144.0 days), and Class III and PMA submissions required the longest review (530.0 and 613.8 days, respectively; all p < 0.001). Established sponsors and domestic manufacturers demonstrated shorter times to authorization than emerging and international counterparts (both p < 0.001). New market entries were concentrated in spinal implants and fixation (n = 1529) and bone graft and augmentation (n = 399). CONCLUSIONS The US spine device landscape has evolved from one dominated by implant and fixation hardware to a more diverse ecosystem defined by navigation, bone graft and augmentation, and other adjunctive technologies, which together now account for nearly half of annual FDA authorizations. Regulatory pathway, device class, sponsor experience, and manufacturer location were each associated with time to FDA decision. These findings provide spine surgeons, innovators, and regulators with a contemporary view of how spine technologies enter clinical practice and highlight areas that may warrant surveillance, particularly in incumbent-dominated categories.

EFEKTIVITAS SELF-STRETCHING TERHADAP PENURUNAN NECK PAIN AKIBAT PENGGUNAAN LAPTOP BAGI MAHASISWA SEMESTER AKHIR DI FAKULTAS KESEHATAN UNIVERSITAS NURUL JADID
abstractText: Penggunaan laptop yang intensif di kalangan mahasiswa khususnya mahasiswa semester akhir, seringkali menjadi penyebab masalah kesehatan seperti nyeri leher (neck pain). Aktivitas yang berlangsung lama dengan posisi tubuh yang tidak ergonomis dapat memicu ketegangan otot leher dan mengganggu kenyamanan. Salah satu intervensi yang dapat dilakukan untuk mengurangi nyeri leher adalah dengan melakukan self-stretching. Menganalisis pengaruh self-stretching terhadap penurunan intensitas nyeri pada mahasiswa yang mengalami nyeri leher. Penelitian ini menggunakan quasi-experiment dengan rancangan pretest dan posttest with control group design. Populasi dalam penelitian ini adalah seluruh mahasiswa semester akhir Fakultas Kesehatan Universitas Nurul Jadid sebanyak 59 orang yang menggunakan laptop dalam aktivitas akademik. Teknik sampling yang digunakan adalah total sampling, sehingga jumlah sampel sebanyak 59 responden yang terdiri dari 30 kelompok intervensi dan 29 kelompok kontrol. Analisis data menggunakan uji Wilcoxon sign test. Berdasarkan penelitian ini, self-stretching berpengaruh terhadap penurunan intensitas nyeri dengan nilai p-value 0.000 (<0.05) pada kelompok intervensi, sedangkan pada kelompok kontrol diperoleh p-value 0.317 (>0.05). Terdapat pengaruh self-stretching terhadap nyeri leher pada mahasiswa semester akhir pengguna laptop pada kelompok yang dilakukan intervensi karena secara self-stretching membantu menurunkan spasme otot dan meningkatkan suplai oksigen ke jaringan sehingga nyeri yang dirasakan berkurang, sedangkan pada kelompok kontrol tidak terdapat pengaruh karena pada kelompok ini tidak dilakukan self-stretching. Abstract Intensive laptop use among students, especially final semester students, often causes health problems such as neck pain. Prolonged activities with non-ergonomic body positions can trigger neck muscle tension and disrupt comfort. One intervention that can be done to reduce neck pain is self-stretching. Analyze the effect of self-stretching on reducing pain intensity in students who experience neck pain. This study used a quasi-experimental design with a pretest and posttest with a control group design. The population in this study were all final semester students of the Faculty of Health, Nurul Jadid University, totaling 59 people who use laptops in academic activities. The sampling technique used was total sampling, so the number of samples was 59 respondents consisting of 30 in the intervention group and 29 in the control group. Data analysis used the Wilcoxon sign test. Based on this study, self-stretching has an effect on reducing pain intensity with a p-value of 0.000 (<0.05) in the intervention group, while in the control group obtained a p-value of 0.317 (>0.05). There is an effect of self-stretching on neck pain in final semester laptop users in the intervention group because self-stretching helps reduce muscle spasms and increases oxygen supply to the tissue so that the pain felt is reduced, while in the control group there is no effect because this group does not do self-stretching.

title: Dietary Modification in an Outpatient With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Hypertension
abstractText: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) accompanied by hypertension is a chronic metabolic disorder requiring individualized nutrition therapy to improve metabolic control and prevent complications. This study aimed to evaluate dietary modification through the Nutrition Care Process in an outpatient with T2DM and hypertension at RSUD Bangil, Pasuruan Regency. A descriptive case study was conducted on a 55-year-old female outpatient diagnosed with T2DM and hypertension. Nutritional care included assessment, diagnosis, intervention, monitoring, and evaluation. The intervention consisted of individualized meal planning, a diabetic diet with sodium and saturated fat restriction, nutrition education, counseling, and modified pumpkin pudding as a healthy snack. Nutritional status, biochemical parameters, dietary intake, knowledge, adherence, and food acceptability were monitored before and after the intervention. Average energy intake reached approximately 100% of estimated requirements. Blood pressure decreased from 138/85 mmHg to 120/79 mmHg. Fasting blood glucose decreased from 172 to 115 mg/dL, while two-hour postprandial blood glucose decreased from 199 to 112 mg/dL. Nutrition knowledge, dietary adherence, and acceptance of the modified diet also improved. Individualized dietary modification combined with continuous nutrition education improved dietary intake, glycemic control, blood pressure, and adherence in this patient.

Photochemical Cross-Organoboron Coupling of Heteroaryl and Alkyl Boronic Acids and Esters
abstractText: Abstract The Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling reaction is a cornerstone of C–C bond formation. However, heteroaryl boronic acids such as pyridyl and quinolyl derivatives remain challenging nucleophiles due to facile protodeboronation. Strategies enabling these substrates are limited to C(sp2)–C(sp2) formation. Efficient and modular C(sp2)–C(sp3) cross-coupling methods that directly employ these substrates remain underdeveloped. Here, we report a cross-organoboron platform that enables direct C(sp2)–C(sp3) bond formation from heteroaryl and alkyl organoboron reagents under visible-light irradiation using Ag2O/TiO2 nanoparticles (NPs). The two organoboron reagents undergo distinct Ag2O NP activations: alkyl boronates undergo single-electron photo-oxidation to generate alkyl radicals while arylboronates undergo transmetalation. Importantly, this method tolerates protodeboronation-prone pyridyl, quinolyl, α-heteroaryl boronic acids, and (hetero)aryl halide-containing substrates, including aryl iodides. High-throughput evaluation across 161 pharmaceutically relevant organoboron substrates identified 113 detectable couplings, and representative examples were validated at preparative scale. This work establishes photochemical cross-organoboron coupling as a complementary approach to classical transition-metal-catalyzed coupling and expands the accessible chemical space of heteroaryl organoboron reagents.

High-yield bio-polyols from sugarcane bagasse: process optimization, structural analysis, and application potential
abstractText: Abstract This research addresses the management of agricultural waste and the partial substitution of petrochemicals in polyurethanes (PUs) by utilizing renewable resources. The present study evaluates, both quantitatively and qualitatively, the feasibility of producing bio-polyols from sugarcane bagasse by polyethylene glycol (PEG 400) as organic solvent. These polyols can be potentially utilized as substitute for petrochemical polyols in elastic PU formulations. The effects of process conditions (temperature, catalyst content, and sugarcane bagasse: solvent ratio) on the bio-polyol yield were evaluated and optimized using response surface methodology through a Box-Behnken design. In addition, at each experimental point, the qualitative characteristics of the resulting bio-polyols, including functional groups, hydroxyl number ( I OH ), acid number ( A n ), molecular weight ( M W ), functionality, viscosity, and polydispersity index (PDI) were determined. The optimal conditions identified by the model determined the most effective experimental parameters as 2 g of sugarcane bagasse, 3.13% catalyst, and a reaction temperature of 161.1 °C. Under these conditions, a polyol yield of 95.6% was achieved, with a prediction error of 4.4%. For the high‑yield samples, I OH ranged from $$\sim$$ ∼ 195 to 233 mg KOH · g⁻ 1 , M W from 3839.27 to 7582.06 g · mol⁻ 1 , functionality between 3.12 and 4, viscosity from 187.5 to 238.4 mPa · s, and PDI between 4.25 and 7.50. These results indicate that the synthesized bio-polyols possess physicochemical characteristics comparable to those reported for polyols used in elastic polyurethane formulations, suggesting their potential suitability for such applications. Overall, the study presents innovative strategies for cost-effective laboratory-scale production of bio-polyols, offering a pathway toward broader industrial adoption.

title: Is the health system working for people? Comparison of adolescent and adult perspectives from the people´s voice survey in Germany
abstractText: Abstract Background People-centred health system performance assessments rely largely on adults, with limited inclusion of adolescents despite their distinct health needs and rights to participate in decisions concerning their health. The People’s Voice Survey is a multi-country, adult-population-representative survey of health system perceptions, but it includes adolescents in the German survey. Germany’s health system offers financial protection and commits to adolescent participation, yet little is known about adolescents’ views of its performance. We aimed to identify adolescent-specific experiences and perspectives by comparing adolescents’ and adults’ experiences and perceptions of health system performance. Methods Population-representative data were collected through an online panel between December 2024 and January 2025. Respondents could choose to take the survey in either German or English. Because adolescents were intentionally oversampled to enable age-group comparisons, we conducted a weighted cross-sectional analysis comparing adolescents (15–19 years) with adults (≥ 20 years) using descriptive statistics and chi-square tests. Variables included self-reported health status, confidence and autonomy in managing health, experiences during care delivery, and perceptions of the health system. Weighted descriptive analyses and chi-square tests were performed. Results The total sample included 2,698 participants: 257 adolescents and 2,441 adults. Compared with adults, adolescents reported better physical but poorer mental health, lower confidence and autonomy in making their own health decisions and communicating concerns to healthcare providers. Compared with adults, adolescents more frequently perceived medical mistakes and receiving care without feeling sufficiently informed, and reported higher levels of unfair or discriminatory treatment. Adults were more critical of the changes to the health system in the past two years and of the system's overall performance. Despite adolescents’ poorer experiences, they had a more positive outlook on the health system's performance. Conclusions Our findings underscore the need to support adolescents' autonomy in making their own health-related decisions and participating in healthcare through age-appropriate communication and opportunities for independent consultations. They also highlight the importance of directly including adolescents in health system performance monitoring, as relying primarily on adult populations may overlook adolescents' unique healthcare experiences and unmet needs.

EXTRACTION AND ANTIOXIDANT ACTIVITY OF CAROTENOID FROM ALGAE Chaetomorpha linum
abstractText: Carotenoids are natural pigments that are found in plants, algae and microorganisms and have antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and disease prevention properties. The effect of various factors on carotenoid extraction from Chaetomorpha linum by static maceration and ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE) was investigated. The effect of five solvents (ethanol, methanol, n-hexane, petroleum ether and acetone), the static extraction time (60, 90, 120, 150 and 180 minutes), the static extraction temperature (30, 40, 50, 60 and 70 °C) and the solid to solvent ratio (1:20, 1:25, 1:30, 1:35 and 1:40 w/v) were systematically investigated. Ultrasound-assisted extraction was examined at solid-to-solvent ratios (1:30, 1:35, 1:40, 1:45 and 1:50 w/v), amplitudes (20, 25, 30, 35 and 40%) and sonication times (5, 10, 15, 20 and 25 minutes). Use of response surface methodology (RSM) followed for the optimisation of the ultrasound-assisted extraction conditions. The antioxidant activity of the extracts obtained was assessed by two different assays: FRAP (ferric reducing antioxidant power) and RP (reducing power). The ultrasound assisted extraction process produced a higher amount of carotenoids (3.016 mg/g DM) than static maceration (2.819 mg/g DM). The RSM optimum was a solid-to-solvent ratio of 1:46 w/w, 36.3% amplitude and 16.39 minutes of sonication. Antioxidant activity was confirmed by both FRAP and RP. The findings indicated that C. linum could be a valuable source of bioactive carotenoids and ultrasound-assisted extraction could enhance the yield and antioxidant capability for food and biomedical uses.

title: Brand forgiveness: a scoping review and agenda for future research
abstractText: Purpose Brand forgiveness reflects consumers’ willingness to maintain or restore relationships with brands following service failures, ethical controversies and marketplace transgressions. The purpose of this study is to conduct a scoping review of the theoretical development, conceptual foundations and future directions of brand forgiveness research. Design/methodology/approach The review synthesizes 80 studies published between 2009 and 2025 using scoping review guidelines and Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-analyses reporting procedures. The analysis examines theoretical foundations, methodological approaches, antecedents, mediators, moderators and outcomes. Findings Brand forgiveness literature is grounded in coping, attribution and justice-based theories of post-transgression evaluation, while relational and identity-based processes remain less developed. The literature identifies firm-, consumer- and brand/communication-related antecedents, along with cognitive, emotional and social mechanisms shaping forgiveness. Methodologically, the field relies largely on experiments and cross-sectional surveys, limiting understanding of forgiveness as a dynamic process. Research limitations/implications The review identifies theoretical, methodological and contextual gaps and proposes directions for advancing brand forgiveness research. Originality/value This review synthesizes fragmented brand forgiveness research and conceptualizes forgiveness as a process involving cognitive interpretation, emotional regulation, moral evaluation and relationship repair.

title: Perfiles poblacionales de enfermedades crónicas no transmisibles, hábitos, características sociodemográficas, vivienda y entorno residencial en Chile: análisis factorial de datos mixtos y conglomerados por K-Prototypes en la ENCAVI 2023-2024
abstractText: Introducción. El enfoque centrado en variables estima el aporte promedio de cada factor a un desenlace, pero no identifica subpoblaciones con combinaciones características de exposiciones y enfermedad. Objetivo. Identificar y caracterizar perfiles poblacionales definidos simultáneamente por enfermedades crónicas no transmisibles (ENT), hábitos, estado nutricional, características sociodemográficas, vivienda y entorno residencial en Chile, y evaluar si la vivienda y el entorno residencial definen un perfil propio. Métodos. Estudio transversal de fuente secundaria con la Encuesta Nacional de Calidad de Vida y Salud (ENCAVI) 2023-2024. Se analizaron 28 variables, 5 continuas y 23 categóricas, en 10.677 casos completos, mediante análisis factorial de datos mixtos (FAMD) y conglomerados por K-Prototypes. El número de conglomerados se eligió según la función de costo, la silueta, los índices de Calinski-Harabasz y Davies-Bouldin, y la estabilidad (índice de Rand ajustado). Las diferencias se evaluaron con chi-cuadrado, ANOVA o Kruskal-Wallis, y tamaños de efecto con intervalos de confianza bootstrap (2.000 remuestreos). Resultados. El 38,6% reportó dos o más ENT. Frente a la multimorbilidad, los mayores tamaños de efecto correspondieron a situación ocupacional, edad y nivel educacional; vivienda y entorno mostraron efectos pequeños. Se retuvieron seis conglomerados: un perfil joven con ventaja socioeconómica, dos perfiles de vejez diferenciados por duración del sueño y carga de dolor, uno de precariedad habitacional y ambiental urbana, uno de obesidad y uno de actividad física declarada muy alta.

title: Advancing neurosurgical practice with augmented reality: a single-center real-world case series with illustrated technical notes
abstractText: OBJECTIVE The aim of this study was to evaluate the real-world application and clinical value of a head-mounted augmented reality (AR) navigation platform across a wide range of neurosurgical pathologies and procedures. METHODS In this real-world retrospective case series, the authors assessed 105 neurosurgical procedures performed by 8 neurosurgeons at a single center from January 2024 to March 2026. A head-mounted AR navigation platform (SurgicalAR, Cranial Navigation, and Spine Navigation; Medivis) was used in all procedures. Video records were available for all cases. Clinical and pathological data, surgical approaches, types of reference frames, and registration methods were systematically collected. The workflow for each surgical approach was characterized in detail. RESULTS This analysis included 105 cases (60 female, mean age 53.5). Cranial surgeries (n = 92, 87.6%) were most common, predominantly for tumors (n = 69, 65.7%), with meningioma (22.9%) and glioblastoma (19.0%) as the leading pathologies. Custom reference frames (n = 57) and surface registration (n = 93) were the most frequently used techniques in cranial navigation. In cranial tumor surgery, gross-total resection was achieved in 62 of 69 cases, supported by multimodal AR planning. In spine surgery, all 34 pedicle screws placed with the Spine Navigation system achieved a Gertzbein-Robbins grade of A. AR was also successfully applied to cerebrovascular, puncture-based, and functional surgery. CONCLUSIONS Head-mounted AR navigation was feasible across diverse procedures, but its value depended on case selection, registration reliability, and workflow. It was most useful for multimodal tumor planning, pedicle screw placement, and percutaneous interventions; conventional navigation or direct anatomical guidance remained necessary when AR accuracy or ergonomics were inadequate. These findings support AR as a significant advancement in future neurosurgical practice.

title: Electrochemically Induced Three-Component Synthesis of Substituted 5-Aminotetrazoles from Isocyanides, Amines, and Azides
abstractText: Abstract A facile one-pot electrochemically induced addition–cyclization reaction of isocyanides, amines, and trimethylsilyl azide (TMSN3) has been established for the construction of diversely substituted 5-aminotetrazoles. This protocol enables efficient C–N and N–N bond formation under mild conditions, avoiding transition-metal catalysts and external oxidants. The reaction exhibits a broad substrate scope and good functional group compatibility, while a gram-scale experiment demonstrates the scalability of this electrochemical protocol.

title: Image-Based Soil Nutrient Prediction Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Models
abstractText: Recent advances in precision agriculture have enabled the use of machine learning and image processing for rapid soil nutrient assessment. This study presents a non-destructive approach for estimating soil nutrient content from digital soil images captured using a camera and analyzed through specialized software. A dataset of 1,500 soil images was processed using color correction, noise reduction, and feature extraction techniques to improve data quality. Five machine learning models, Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM), and a Stacking Regressor, were evaluated for predicting nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium levels. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based deep learning model was served as a benchmark. No single model was best for every nutrient and metric. For nitrogen, GBM achieved the lowest test MAE (0.1652), whereas the Stacking Regressor achieved the highest test R² (0.9886). For potassium, Random Forest achieved the lowest test MAE (0.0051), whereas XGBoost achieved the highest test R² (0.9999). For phosphorus, XGBoost achieved both the lowest test MAE (0.1558) and the highest test R² (0.9929). Thus, the best-performing model depends on the nutrient and evaluation metric. Further validation using independent field datasets is required to establish robustness under diverse environmental conditions.

title: Artificial intelligence–based tumor detection using stimulated Raman histology in patients undergoing neurosurgical biopsies
abstractText: OBJECTIVE Intraoperative confirmation of diagnostic tumor tissue is critical in neurosurgical biopsies, particularly in stereotactic procedures, in which sampling error remains a major limitation. Stimulated Raman histology (SRH) enables rapid, label-free tissue imaging directly in the operating room. This study aimed to evaluate the performance of intraoperative SRH combined with artificial intelligence (AI)–based tumor detection using a CE (Conformité Européenne)–certified algorithm under routine clinical conditions, with a focus on scan-level analysis and the impact of tissue heterogeneity. METHODS The authors conducted a retrospective single-center study including all consecutive patients who underwent neurosurgical biopsy with intraoperative SRH imaging between December 2020 and October 2025. All acquired SRH scans were analyzed using the Glioma Reveal algorithm, which provides a probabilistic analysis of tumor cell presence. Diagnostic performance at the scan level (defined as a specific region of interest [ROI]) was assessed. After SRH analysis, each tissue sample was investigated by routine histopathological analysis. For statistical analysis, all cases were categorized into three groups based on their final histopathological diagnosis: 1) common tumor entities, 2) rare tumor entities, and 3) nonneoplastic lesions. In discordant cases between AI-based classification and histopathological assessment, a board-certified neuropathologist performed a secondary review of the corresponding SRH images to assess whether the AI prediction was morphologically plausible. RESULTS Analysis of 204 SRH scans obtained in 89 patients using the Glioma Reveal algorithm showed an initial overall accuracy of 80.9% for tumor tissue detection. After expert review of the misclassified cases, accuracy increased to 94.1%. In the group of gliomas and lymphomas (70 patients, 168 scans), the initial accuracy was 81.5% (sensitivity 78.8%, specificity 100.0%). Expert review confirmed that 80.6% (25 scans) of false-negative results were morphologically correct within the specific ROI, despite global specimen positivity. After correction for these cases, accuracy increased to 96.4%. In rare tumors (8 patients, 20 scans), diagnostic accuracy rose from 90.0% to 100.0% after expert review. In nonneoplastic lesions (11 patients, 16 scans), initial accuracy remained at 62.5% regardless of expert review due to reactive mimics. CONCLUSIONS SRH imaging using the Glioma Reveal algorithm provides rapid intraoperative confirmation of representative tumor tissue during biopsy. Although automated performance is robust, intraspecimen heterogeneity and spatial sampling differences significantly impact diagnostic metrics and should be taken into account.

abstractText: The selection of health facilities for childbirth is important to support safe delivery. This study aimed to determine the factors associated with the selection of health facilities for childbirth among third-trimester pregnant women in the working area of Tegal Buleud Public Health Center, Sukabumi Regency. This quantitative study used a cross-sectional design. The population consisted of 223 third-trimester pregnant women, with a sample of 143 respondents selected through simple random sampling. Data were collected using questionnaires and analyzed using univariate and bivariate analyses with the Chi-Square test. The results showed significant associations between education (p=0.020), JKN ownership (p=0.020; OR=2.833), knowledge (p<0.001; OR=6.480), accessibility (p<0.001; OR=9.707), and culture and beliefs (p<0.001; OR=4.949) and the selection of health facilities for childbirth. Age (p=0.308), occupation (p=0.586), and income (p=0.549) were not significantly associated. Accessibility had the highest OR. In conclusion, education, JKN ownership, knowledge, accessibility, and culture and beliefs were associated with the selection of health facilities for childbirth. Improving the utilization of health facilities requires education, better accessibility, financial protection, and family- and culturally sensitive approaches.

title: Acoustical Materials from Conventional to Cutting-Edge Innovations─An Overview
abstractText: Abstract With rapid urbanization and industrial expansion, noise pollution has escalated into a pervasive environmental and public health crisis. Thus, an imperative need arises for both advanced sound mitigation strategies and, especially, a fundamental shift toward sustainability to meet pressing worldwide environmental policies. The overview critically examines, unlike the already published reviews, the broad spectrum of AMs─from established conventional options to cutting-edge innovations─while consistently evaluating them through the lenses of working mechanisms, acoustic performance, and holistic sustainability (including manufacturing and life-cycle considerations). For applications where blocking airborne sound is the primary objective, natural materials with higher density and mass, such as denser types of wood or composites incorporating mass-enhancing components, should be prioritized because the acoustical properties of natural materials as soundproofing materials are influenced by a complex interplay of factors (density, mass, porosity, air permeability, thickness, internal structure, resonant frequencies, surface area, and texture). This paper systematically explores the fundamental principles of sound interaction with materials, classifying traditional, natural, hybrid, and emerging smart materials and metamaterials. The following discussion explores key performance metrics, practical applications, and the inherent challenges and future directions in the field, striving to offer a holistic perspective on the ongoing quest for effective, durable, and truly sustainable acoustic solutions. Therefore, this overview is intended to be an exhaustive, comprehensive, and valuable tool for engineers and researchers in the field of acoustic materials, with real help for saving cost and time throughout the design process. Such an overview covering all acoustic material types with elements of sustainability and future perspectives has never been reported before.

title: Is the surgeon or hospital a larger cost driver for lumbar fusion? A hierarchical Bayesian approach using time-driven activity-based costing
abstractText: OBJECTIVE Considerable variability exists in lumbar fusion outcomes, with prior studies demonstrating significant differences across both surgeons and hospitals. However, similar analyses for cost are lacking, making it unclear whether surgeons or hospitals are larger cost drivers for lumbar fusion, particularly in multihospital health systems. Therefore, the aim of this study was to perform a risk-adjusted time-driven activity-based costing (TDABC) analysis for single-level lumbar fusion to compare overall cost variance between surgeons and hospitals in a multihospital health system. METHODS This retrospective cohort study included single-level lumbar fusions performed (2020–2024) at a healthcare network encompassing several quaternary and community hospitals. TDABC was used to calculate the true intraoperative cost (not charges or reimbursement) of each case. Hierarchical Bayesian regression models were fit for total cost, and its primary drivers: supply cost and personnel cost. Random effects were specified for surgeon and hospital site, while fixed covariates included patient- and procedure-specific factors. Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling was performed to generate posterior draws for all model parameters, from which posterior medians and 95% Bayesian credible intervals (BCIs) were reported. RESULTS This analysis included 943 lumbar fusions performed by 23 surgeons across 9 hospitals. The mean total cost of surgery was $23,106 ± $10,475, driven by supplies (mean $20,344 ± $10,010) and personnel (mean $2755 ± $1019). Nonoverlapping BCIs demonstrated that between-surgeon variance was greater than between-site variance for both total cost and supply cost. Specifically, surgeon-level variance was 30-times greater than site-level variance for total cost (median 29.8, 95% BCI 1.4–10,756.4) and 53-times greater for supply cost (median 52.5, 95% BCI 2.0–28,374.7). Furthermore, for each 1 standard deviation difference between surgeons, there was a 29.9% (95% BCI 18.2–48.5) increase in total cost and a 35.2% (95% BCI 21.1–57.3) increase in supply cost, whereas comparable differences between sites were associated with only 5.5% (95% BCI 0.3–23.8) and 4.8% (95% BCI 0.2–23.4) increases in cost, respectively. In contrast, surgeon and site contributions were comparable for personnel cost, with overlapping BCIs. CONCLUSIONS In cases of single-level lumbar fusions performed at a multihospital health system, variation in cost between surgeons was 30-times greater than variation between hospitals, although residual/unexplained variance was considerable. These hypothesis-generating findings might enhance physician awareness of cost drivers and practice heterogeneity. However, additional research is necessary to identify sources of unexplained variance, as well as to integrate costs with outcomes to determine whether cost variability represents value or waste.

Ekstraksi Data Formulir Downtime Tulisan Tangan Menggunakan Vision-Language Model Qwen2.5-VL Lokal pada Sistem Pencatatan Produksi PT Intiroda Makmur
abstractText: Daily downtime records for the wire drawing process at PT Intiroda Makmur were written on paper forms and then retyped into a Visual Basic 6 desktop application available on a single office computer. Paper cannot be removed because occupational safety rules restrict phones near the machines. During an internship (5 July–14 August 2026), a web-based recording system was built on the company’s existing SQL Server databases, together with a module that extracts form data from photos using the Qwen2.5-VL 3B vision-language model running locally through Ollama, so no production data leaves the intranet. Extraction runs in two stages: a full-page photo for the header (Canny edge detection, perspective correction, CLAHE) and a close-up of the 48-cell downtime grid, rectified by a three-point affine transform. An ink-ratio gate skips empty cells before the model is called, prompts restrict the model to transcription, outputs are validated with Pydantic, machine codes are chosen only from the official master list, and operator names are matched with bidirectional string similarity (threshold 70%). A review screen keeps a human in the loop before data are saved. The ink-ratio gate reduced Section 2 processing time from 150–156 s to 2.0–33.6 s depending on the number of filled cells. All 45 unit tests (165 assertions) and 16 black-box scenarios passed; reading accuracy was evaluated qualitatively and still requires quantitative measurement.

title: A Study on Basic Test Parameters for Performance of Class D Extinguishers Against Lithium Metal Fires
abstractText: The industrial demand for lithium metal is increasing rapidly; however, neither domestic nor international Class D fire extinguisher standards currently include performance test criteria specifically validated for lithium metal fires. In this study, the Korean Class D fire extinguisher standard was compared with UL 711 and ISO 7165 standards to derive candidate test conditions, and the combustion and extinguishing behavior of lithium was investigated on the basis of fire tests performed using lithium foil. Under the present test conditions, lithium foil fires showed a low heat release rate but sustained high temperatures over a prolonged period, and reignition triggered by deep-seated residual heat was identified as the principal hazard. A commercial copper powder-based Class D metal fire extinguisher by itself was insufficient to suppress reignition. However, the addition of excess copper powder led to a decrease in the heat release rate and temperature while suppressing reignition. Accordingly, the basic test parameters for evaluating the lithium fire-extinguishing performance—i.e., the specimen quantity, test frame dimensions, agent discharge time, and extinguishment criteria—were examined as candidate conditions for future verification studies.

title: Water Demand Prediction and Optimal Redesign of Water Distribution Networks Considering Future Environmental Changes
abstractText: Future demographic, industrial, and climate changes increase uncertainty in water distribution network operations. This study analyzes future water demand and hydraulic performance in Paju City from 2021 to 2050 and proposes an optimal network redesign strategy. Changes in unit water demand due to the increasing proportion of one- and two-person households and industrial demand growth were considered together with pipeline aging and extreme climate conditions. Scenario-based hydraulic analysis using EPANET was integrated with genetic algorithm-based optimization. The results show that total water demand will increase despite the eventual population decline, mainly due to increased unit demand. Extreme climate conditions had a greater impact on hydraulic performance than changes in demand or pipeline aging, resulting in 253 pressure-deficient nodes by 2050. Optimization showed that selective expansion of small- and medium-diameter pipes effectively mitigated pressure deficiencies. The proposed framework supports long-term water distribution network operation and redesign under future demographic, industrial, and climate changes.
