title: Container-surface-guided dual-task learning for defect detection in complex port scenes
abstractText: Automatic container defect inspection in complex port environments is hindered by substantial scale variation and defect-like interference from non-container regions. This article presents CSG-YOLO, a container-surface-guided dual-task framework that jointly learns five-class defect detection and container-surface segmentation. Its scale-tuned feature fusion module adapts multi-level neck features to defects of different spatial extents, while mask-guided cross-task interaction bidirectionally exchanges the learned surface prior and defect cues between the task heads. Center-to-container consistency and edge-aware mask refinement losses respectively encourage defect-center coverage and surface-boundary consistency. On a single-terminal dataset of 4,000 distinct port images containing 4,480 defect instances, CSG-YOLO-N achieves mean scores of 58.1 average precision (AP), 93.0 AP50, and 65.0 AP75 across three independent training runs, with 16.3 GFLOPs. Compared with YOLOv12-N, it improves these metrics by 2.4, 3.2, and 4.1 points, respectively, while reducing mean overall missed detection rate from 6.4% to 5.7%, false positives per image from 0.19 to 0.11, and outside-region-of-interest (ROI) detection ratio from 1.8% to 0.2%. It also obtains a mean Surface intersection over union of 76.7%. These results support the effectiveness of explicit container-surface modeling for defect detection and suppression of spatially invalid detections on the evaluated dataset. Generalization to other port environments remains to be established.

title: Consumer responses to conflicting brand news in digital feeds
abstractText: Purpose This study aims to explain how negative brand information gains influence when presented alongside positive information in digital feeds. This study addresses a gap in brand-crisis research, which has not traced how competing cues capture attention, activate violation-specific emotions, alter corresponding legitimacy beliefs and persist over time. Design/methodology/approach Three studies test a process model grounded in negativity bias and cognitive appraisal theory. Study 1 uses within-participant eye tracking (n = 117). Study 2 combines eye tracking and survey measures in a randomised experiment (n = 285). Study 3 uses a three-wave longitudinal experiment (n = 279 at T3). Findings Negative information attracted more visual attention than concurrent positive information. Greater negative attention share (NAS) intensified contempt towards worker-treatment violations and disgust towards integrity violations, which, respectively, reduced perceived employee care and ethical integrity. Anger and sadness did not mediate these relationships, while social identification strengthened both pathways. Legitimacy threats also produced larger, more persistent changes in the affected legitimacy belief than in overall brand evaluation. Research limitations/implications Brand-crisis research should treat attention as an early selection mechanism and distinguish discrete moral emotions, legitimacy domains and evaluative layers. Practical implications Brand responses should address the specific obligation under threat. Positive communication may support overall brand evaluation but may not restore beliefs about employee care or ethical integrity once directly challenged. Originality/value The findings of this study extend negativity bias from a final weighting effect to a sequence involving attentional competition, moral appraisal and layered evaluation.

title: Resepsi Audiens terhadap Konten Storytelling Boombayah pada Tiktok @Octatannn
abstractText: TikTok storytelling presents personal and relational issues through brief audiovisual narratives that invite diverse interpretations from viewers. This study examines audience reception of the Boombayah episode “Kejanggalan Pacaran Sama Hafidz” published by the TikTok account @octatannn. The research employed a descriptive qualitative approach and Stuart Hall’s encoding-decoding framework. Data were collected through observation of the selected content and comments, structured interviews with five active viewers aged 18–25, and documentation. The data were condensed, categorized into dominant-hegemonic, negotiated, and oppositional positions, presented thematically, and validated through source and technique triangulation. The findings show that one informant occupied the dominant-hegemonic position by fully accepting the creator’s preferred meaning concerning honesty, communication, manipulation, and the decision to end an unhealthy relationship. Three informants occupied negotiated positions: they accepted the central warning about toxic relationships and digital privacy but questioned the absence of legal consequences, the simplified closing advice, and the one-sided construction of social-media narratives. One informant occupied the oppositional position by rejecting the suitability of publishing the story without an age warning and replacing the creator’s message with a normative emphasis on mature communication and legal accountability. Personal experience and values or beliefs were the two principal factors shaping these positions. The results confirm that TikTok audiences actively interpret, adjust, or reject messages rather than merely receiving them. Creators should therefore provide contextual warnings, acknowledge alternative resolutions, and consider ethical responsibility when presenting sensitive relationship narratives.

A Unified Phosgene-Free Carbonylation Using CO2 for the Synthesis of Ureas, Carbamates, Carbonates, Amides, and Formamides
abstractText: Abstract Phosgene remains a privileged reagent for carbonylation; however, its extreme toxicity and stringent regulatory controls often restrict its routine and broad application. Herein, we describe a unified CO2-based carbonylation platform for the synthesis of ureas, (thio)carbamates, (thio)carbonates, amides, and formamides under mild, metal-free conditions. The method employs readily available phosphorus(V) activators to generate transient phosphorus-activated carbonyl species that selectively react with amines, alcohols, thiols, hydrides, and organometallic reagents, enabling a one-pot, three-component protocol that telescopes multi-step phosgene-based sequences into a single operation. This approach eliminates the need for phosgene and other preactivated carbonylating reagents. Mechanistic studies are most consistent with the involvement of a transient phosphorus-mediated carbonylating species, conceptually analogous to electrophilic carbonyl transfer in biological systems, although its precise identity remains unresolved. The synthetic utility of the platform is demonstrated by the 25 g synthesis of the anticancer drug sorafenib using POCl3 as the activator. By harnessing CO2 as a C1 synthon, this strategy addresses a long-standing challenge in electrophilic carbonylation and provides an operationally simple and complementary alternative to phosgene-based methods.

title: Pengaruh Aksesibilitas terhadap Minat Berkunjung Ulang Wisatawan di Desa Wisata Maligi Kabupaten Pasaman Barat
abstractText: Accessibility plays an important role in tourism destination development, but road conditions and the ease of travel to Maligi Tourism Village in Pasaman Barat Regency still require attention. This study aimed to analyze the effect of accessibility on tourists’ revisit intention and describe tourists’ assessments of the destination’s accessibility. The study employed a quantitative approach with a causal associative design. The sample comprised 314 respondents selected from a population of 1,227 individuals through non-probability sampling using a purposive sampling method. Data were collected using a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire distributed in person and through Google Forms. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS. The analysis showed that accessibility had a positive and significant relationship with revisit intention, with a path coefficient of 0.344 (t = 4.898; p < 0.001). Meanwhile, the descriptive assessment of accessibility yielded a mean score of 2.84, which was categorized as low in this study. These findings indicate that accessibility should be prioritized in the development of Maligi Tourism Village, given tourists’ ratings that remain low and its relationship with revisit intention. This study provides an empirical basis for destination managers to evaluate road conditions, transportation convenience, directional signs, and access to information as part of efforts to improve accessibility and support tourists’ revisit intention.

title: LESS-PseU: A Language Model-Enhanced Semistacking Framework for RNA Pseudouridine Site Prediction
abstractText: Abstract Accurate prediction of RNA pseudouridine (Ψ) sites remains challenging because existing models often struggle to integrate interpretable handcrafted features with high-dimensional contextual representations from pretrained genomic language models. To address this issue, we propose LESS-PseU, a language model-enhanced semistacking framework that fuses the predicted probability features of primary learners with DNABERT2 embeddings for multiple species Ψ site prediction. Specifically, we first built three primary learners based on three kinds of hand-crafted features, including one-hot, k-mer, and nucleotide chemical property features. Instead of training a primary learner based on the embeddings extracted from DNABERT2, the embeddings were directly concatenated with the predicted probabilities of the three primary learners as the input features for a Logistic Regression meta-learner for final prediction. Under a leakage-aware cross-validation setting, our model was validated on the training sets of three species. Furthermore, on independent test sets from human, mouse, and yeast, LESS-PseU achieved AUC values of 0.9069, 0.8833, and 0.8820, respectively, which were higher than those of the compared models. A Friedman test indicated an overall difference (p = 0.029). Paired DeLong tests further showed that the AUC improvements over Meta-PseU were significant for the human and mouse data sets, while those over PseU-ST were significant for all three species. Ablation analysis, fusion-strategy comparison, and pretrained language-model comparison further demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. Additional evaluations on m5C and m7G benchmarks provided preliminary evidence that the framework may be applicable to other RNA modification prediction tasks.

title: Bi(OTf)3-Catalyzed Diastereoselective Three-Component Povarov Reaction of Aminoquinones toward Tetrahydroquinolinequinones
abstractText: Abstract We have developed a Bi(OTf)3-catalyzed three-component Povarov reaction of aminoquinones, aldehydes, and olefins that provides straightforward, one-step access to highly substituted 1,2,3,4-tetrahydroquinolinequinones in isolated yields of up to 96%, with diastereoselectivities ranging from 1.6:1 to >20:1. Mechanistic studies using E- and Z-alkene probes support a stepwise cationic pathway rather than a concerted cycloaddition, which rationalizes the observed stereochemical outcomes. The synthetic utility is further highlighted by subsequent oxidative dehydrogenation to afford quinolinequinone derivatives, a class of molecules of significant biological relevance.

title: What enables the safe prescription and monitoring of morphine for chronic breathlessness? Insights from a Normalisation Process Theory-informed implementation survey and interviews with clinicians
abstractText: Abstract Background Shortness of breath affects almost 10% of the general population, in particular people with lung or heart disease receiving palliative care. Reducing breathlessness by implementing effective pharmacological and non-pharmacological treatment is vital for relieving this physical and mental suffering in chronic illness. This mixed-methods implementation study (conducted as part of the Morphine and BrEathLessness trial (MABEL) of the clinical effectiveness and safety of regular low-dose oral modified release morphine) investigates how the experiences, attitudes and practices of clinicians affect the prescription of morphine for the symptomatic reduction of chronic breathlessness. Methods Mixed-methods survey and interview study with clinicians at participating trial sites, informed by Normalisation Process Theory: 1) Learning Needs Assessment survey to provide early indication of clinicians’ experiences and knowledge 2) Normalisation Measurement instrument (NoMAD) survey at two time points to measure extent to which morphine prescribing fitted with current practice 3) Semi-structured interviews with clinicians to explore perspectives about safe morphine use. Results Participants: Learning Needs Assessment (n=75, Doctors 43%, Nurses 51%, Other/not stated 6%), NoMAD 1 (n=64; Doctors 45%, Nurses 50%, Other 5%), NoMAD 2 (n=27; Doctors 41%, Nurses 52%, Other 9%), interviews (n=8, Doctors n=5, Nurses n=3). Learning Needs Assessment: two-thirds agreed they had learning needs about use of morphine for breathlessness. NoMAD surveys: 92% viewed morphine for breathlessness as a legitimate part of their role, but only 36% thought sufficient training about its use was provided. 81% stated they could integrate the use of morphine for breathlessness into their existing work, but only 39% had confidence in colleagues to do so. Interviews supported NoMAD findings and provided a richer understanding of how communication and co-ordination across settings and specialisms underpinned implementation. Conclusions Morphine prescription for breathlessness management is seen by clinicians as a legitimate part of their role. However, a lack of training opportunities, resources, and confidence in the skills of others impede successful implementation. Robust communication and shared decision-making between clinicians, and between clinicians and patients, across settings and specialisms can support the delivery of a safe, effective approach when morphine is being considered for breathlessness. Operational efficiency in blood component production: time-driven process mapping study from a national blood service in sub-Saharan Africa
abstractText: Abstract Background Efficient blood service operations are critical to safe blood supply in low- and middle-income countries (LMIC). Process mapping provides a systematic approach to understanding operational complexity and identifying inefficiencies. This study aims to map the blood component production cycle at a national blood service. Methods We conducted a detailed process mapping exercise across four stages of blood production: donor recruitment, blood collection, blood processing and testing, and storage and dispatch. We enumerated client pathways and recorded active process times at each stage, guided by a time-driven data collection framework. The e-Delphyn blood donor management system supported data capture at static and mobile collection sites. Results The blood component production cycle comprises four sequential stages, generating 31 distinct client pathways at the donor recruitment stage alone, reflecting substantial operational complexity. Donor recruitment active organization time ranged from 6 to 148 min, depending on the mobilization approach and site. Blood collection followed a consistent patient flow regardless of site, with optimal completion time of ~ 31 min. Under minimum batch conditions, blood processing and testing required a minimum of 113 min. Blood component production times varied substantially from 15 min for packed red blood cells via platelet-rich plasma extraction to a minimum of 555 min for cryoprecipitate. Conclusions Process mapping revealed significant operational complexity within the non-remunerated volunteer donor-based blood component production cycle. By embedding process times into the mapping framework, this study demonstrated how variability in each blood processing stage shapes overall system efficiency. These time-driven insights provide the first granular, evidence-based foundation for informing efficiency analysis and resource allocation across Sub-Saharan Africa and other LMIC blood services. The association between preoperative cervical degeneration in adult patients with spinal deformity and poor postoperative cervical sagittal alignment after thoracolumbar deformity correction
abstractText: OBJECTIVE Thoracolumbar (TL) deformity correction in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis has been shown to promote favorable compensatory cervical alignment changes, often restoring cervical lordosis. However, the influence of cervical degeneration on postoperative cervical alignment in adult spinal deformity (ASD) remains unclear. This study investigated the effect of preoperative cervical disc degeneration on postoperative cervical sagittal alignment (CSA) following TL deformity correction in ASD. METHODS One hundred eighty-one patients with ASD who underwent deformity correction from the cervicothoracic junction (upper instrumented vertebra [UIV] between C7 and T4) to the lumbosacral spine (lowest instrumented vertebra between L1 and S1 or the ilium) with a minimum 2-year follow-up were analyzed. Preoperative cervical MRI was evaluated using the Miyazaki classification system to grade intervertebral disc degeneration. Patients were stratified into 3 groups: group 1, minimal degeneration; group 2, 1–2 severely degenerated discs (grade ≥ IV); and group 3, ≥ 3 severely degenerated discs. CSA (kyphosis vs lordosis), C2–7 sagittal vertical axis (cSVA), and T1 slope (T1S) were measured preoperatively, immediately postoperatively, and at 1- and 2-year follow-up. Optimal CSA was defined as within 20° of the T1S (T1S-CSA mismatch < 20°). RESULTS At baseline, groups 1–3 demonstrated no significant differences in CSA, T1S, cSVA, or TL alignment. Postoperatively and through 2 years of follow-up, groups 2 and 3 demonstrated significantly worse CSA compared with group 1. Patients in group 1 maintained improved cervical alignment and T1S-CSA matching, whereas groups 2 and 3 either preserved or worsened their preoperative malalignment. On multivariable logistic regression, the odds of achieving T1S-CSA mismatch < 20° were 81% lower in group 2 (OR 0.198, p < 0.05) and 91% lower in group 3 (OR 0.087, p < 0.0001; area under the receiver operating characteristic curve = 0.88). On multivariable linear regression, each severely degenerated cervical disc (grade ≥ IV) was associated with a 1.4° increase in T1S-CSA mismatch (β = 1.4, R 2 = 0.75, p < 0.0001). CONCLUSIONS Patients with ASD and minimal cervical degeneration experienced sustained reciprocal improvements in cervical alignment for up to 2 years after TL deformity correction that included a UIV between C7 and T4. In contrast, patients with preexisting cervical degeneration were more likely to maintain or worsen their malalignment. Preoperative cervical MRI should be routinely performed to assess degeneration during surgical planning.

abstractText: The Indonesian government is actively working towards achieving comprehensive waste management through a range of strategies implemented across different regions. The decline in waste management can be attributed to the fast-paced rise in population, urbanization, and industrial consumption across various sectors. This research focuses on identifying the primary obstacles of waste management in Sleman Regency. It involves analyzing geospatial data through GIS techniques to determine suitable locations for new waste landfills. In addition, it strives to present all-encompassing solutions that consider both environmental and economic factors at the individual and community levels. The research method employed is a combination of quantitative and qualitative approaches, involving the collection and analysis of data from various sources such as maps, observations, interviews, and document searches. The study findings highlight several key challenges in waste management in Sleman, including the need to address increasing waste volumes, raise public awareness, improve infrastructure, strengthen regulations and law enforcement, secure adequate funding, foster collaboration, and adapt to changing community consumption patterns. Additionally, the study identifies a suitable landfill location in Madu Rejo Village, Prambanan District, spanning 4.1 hectares, which meets national standards (SNI) and feasibility norms (SKL). Lastly, the study suggests an alternative solution that integrates waste banks, TPST3R, with TPA, and emphasizes the importance of community education in addressing these issues. Managing waste in a methodical, thorough, and sustainable manner from start to finish (from households to waste treatment facilities) brings economic advantages, promotes community health and environmental safety, and has the potential to influence people's actions.

A Unified Analytical Framework for Modal Analysis of Beams with Elastic Supports and End Masses
abstractText: Predicting vibration in beamlike structures with non-ideal supports remain a significant engineering challenge. Classical beam models usually assume perfectly rigid boundaries. Real structures, however, contain flexible supports and attached end components that modify the dynamic response. This study develops a unified analytical framework for the free vibration analysis of Euler–Bernoulli beams with elastic restraints and lumped end masses. The formulation incorporates translational stiffness, rotational stiffness, and rotary inertia within a compact and physically transparent model. Frequency-dependent boundary conditions are assembled into a concise 4 × 4 characteristic matrix. Classical free–free, clamped–free, and clamped–clamped conditions emerge naturally as limiting cases. MATLAB is employed to extract the natural frequencies and mode shapes. Validation is performed through three-dimensional (3D) ANSYS simulations using quadratic HEX20 solid elements. The results demonstrate strong agreement between analytical and finite element predictions across a wide range of stiffness and mass parameters. Mesh convergence studies confirm stable and reliable solutions for the first six bending modes. The findings clearly illustrate that boundary flexibility and end inertia substantially influence modal characteristics and vibration behavior. In addition, the proposed formulation maintains analytical simplicity while capturing realistic structural behavior with high accuracy. The framework also provides a reliable benchmark for validating advanced numerical models and future experimental investigations. Overall, the proposed approach offers an accurate, computationally efficient, and practical tool for vibration prediction and engineering design of realistic beam structures.

title: Remotely delivered support to promote physical activity behaviour change for women aged 50 years and over: study protocol for the Active Women over 50 hybrid type I effectiveness-implementation randomised controlled trial
abstractText: Abstract Background Physical activity has health benefits but women in midlife years often face complex challenges to regular participation and could benefit from targeted support. The pilot-tested Active Women over 50 behaviour change program, was acceptable and feasible for supporting choice-based physical activity among women aged 50 years and over. This trial aims to establish the impact of the remotely-delivered Active Women over 50 program on physical activity among women aged 50 years and over compared with a waitlist control group. Methods This hybrid type I effectiveness-implementation randomised controlled trial ( n = 1000) will be conducted among community-dwelling women aged 50 years and over across NSW Australia, half living in rural/regional areas. Participants will set two physical activity SMART goals with a health coach and then be randomised to receive the Active Women over 50 program, or to a waitlist control group. The Active Women over 50 program will include (1) two empowerment-focused telephone health coaching sessions; (2) behaviour-change messages delivered by email or SMS text as preferred; (3) program-specific website containing information, tips and strategies and inspirational peer stories; and (4) private moderated Facebook group. The control group will be waitlisted to receive the Active Women over 50 program 6 months post-randomisation. The primary outcome will be average daily steps measured with the ActiGraph accelerometer at baseline and 6-months post-randomisation. Secondary outcomes include device-measured and self-reported physical activity, falls, quality of life, action and coping planning, process and implementation and scalability measures, and health utilisation. All analyses will be pre-planned and conducted while blinded to group allocation and will consider participant and geographical characteristics. An economic analysis will estimate cost-effectiveness and cost-utility of the intervention compared to no intervention. Discussion This hybrid type 1 effectiveness-implementation trial testing a flexible, remotely-delivered behaviour change intervention designed with consumer input will establish the impact on physical activity among women aged 50 + years living across diverse geographical settings. The trial design will also collect secondary implementation, scalability and cost outcomes to provide important information to stakeholder groups such as community groups, professionals, policymakers, funding bodies. Numerical Evaluation of a Bottom Plate Countermeasure Against Pipeline Uplift in Liquefiable Ground
abstractText: Pipelines buried in liquefiable ground are vulnerable to uplift, which can cause serious damage. Various countermeasures have been proposed to mitigate pipeline uplift, some of which have adverse effects. Prior centrifuge model tests have shown that a bottom plate countermeasure (BPC), in which a horizontal plate is installed beneath the pipe, effectively suppresses uplift. In this study, finite element method analyses were performed to examine the behavior of the surrounding soil under BPC application and to evaluate the effects of plate length, burial depth, ground conditions, and input acceleration. The analyses showed that the BPC enlarged the soil region resisting pipeline uplift by extending the shear surface deeper into the horizontal plate and farther outward from the pipe. Because of this resistance mechanism, the BPC was particularly effective under shallow burial conditions, where reduced overburden load made pipelines more susceptible to uplift. Analyses considering field pipeline installation practices, with the pipeline embedded in a sand-backfilled trench within non-liquefiable native ground, also showed that uplift with the BPC was limited to approximately 1 mm or less, demonstrating strong uplift suppression. These results confirm the applicability of the BPC and provide a basis for future field implementation.

Peran Motivasi Dan Kepuasan Kerja Dalam Meningkatkan Kinerja Pegawai
abstractText: Employee performance is a key factor in improving the effectiveness of public service delivery. However, achieving optimal employee performance remains influenced by several factors, particularly work motivation and job satisfaction. This study aims to examine the effects of work motivation and job satisfaction on employee performance at the Class I Immigration Office TPI Denpasar. A quantitative research approach was employed involving 50 employees selected through proportionate random sampling based on the Slovin formula. Primary data were collected using a structured questionnaire and analyzed using multiple linear regression. The findings indicate that work motivation has a positive and significant effect on employee performance. Job satisfaction also has a positive and significant effect on employee performance. Furthermore, work motivation and job satisfaction simultaneously have a significant influence on employee performance. These findings suggest that strengthening employee motivation and job satisfaction is essential for improving employee performance within public sector organizations. The results provide practical implications for the management of the Class I Immigration Office TPI Denpasar in developing policies aimed at enhancing employee motivation and job satisfaction to achieve better organizational performance.

title: PENGARUH EFFLEURAGE DENGAN AROMATERAPI JAHE MERAH TERHADAP DISMENORE PRIMER PADA REMAJA DI POLTEKKES KEMENKES MALANG
abstractText: Dismenore primer merupakan nyeri yang terjadi saat menstruasi dan dapat mengganggu aktivitas sehari-hari, termasuk konsentrasi belajar, kegiatan akademik, dan aktivitas fisik. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh pijat effleurage dengan aromaterapi jahe merah (Zingiber officinale) terhadap dismenore primer pada remaja di Poltekkes Kemenkes Malang Kampus IV. Penelitian ini menggunakan desain pre-eksperimental dengan pendekatan one-group pretest–posttest. Sampel terdiri atas 41 mahasiswa tingkat I, II, dan III yang dipilih menggunakan teknik purposive sampling berdasarkan kriteria inklusi dan eksklusi yang telah ditetapkan. Pengukuran dilakukan sebelum dan sesudah intervensi menggunakan instrumen WaLIDD (Working Ability, Location, Intensity, Days of Pain, Dysmenorrhea). Data dianalisis menggunakan uji Wilcoxon signed-rank dengan tingkat signifikansi 0,05. Hasil analisis menunjukkan nilai p kurang dari 0,001, yang mengindikasikan adanya perbedaan skor dismenore sebelum dan sesudah intervensi yang bermakna secara statistik. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa pemberian pijat effleurage dengan aromaterapi jahe merah berpotensi menjadi salah satu pilihan intervensi nonfarmakologis untuk membantu mengatasi dismenore primer. Penelitian selanjutnya disarankan untuk mengevaluasi kandungan minyak jahe merah serta menguji intervensi ini dengan desain yang melibatkan kelompok kontrol. Kata kunci : Effleurage, Dismenor, Remaja Abstract Primary dysmenorrhea is menstrual pain that may interfere with daily activities, including concentration, academic performance, and physical activity. This study aimed to analyze the effect of effleurage massage combined with red ginger aromatherapy on primary dysmenorrhea among adolescents at Poltekkes Kemenkes Malang, Campus IV. A pre-experimental study with a one-group pretest–posttest design was conducted. The sample consisted of 41 students from the first, second, and third academic years who were selected using purposive sampling based on predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. Dysmenorrhea was assessed before and after the intervention using the WaLIDD (Working Ability, Location, Intensity, Days of Pain, Dysmenorrhea) instrument. Data were analyzed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, with a significance level of 0.05. The analysis showed a p-value of less than 0.001, indicating a statistically significant difference in dysmenorrhea scores before and after the intervention. These findings suggest that effleurage massage combined with red ginger aromatherapy may be a potential non-pharmacological option for managing primary dysmenorrhea. Future studies should investigate the chemical composition of red ginger essential oil and evaluate the intervention using a study design that includes a control group.

title: Antimicrobial Peptide Databases and Prediction Tools: Toward a Standard Evaluation Framework
abstractText: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has a profound impact on animal and human health and is associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, and public health costs. There is a clear need to develop novel, effective antibiotic agents, which can overcome the current AMR crisis. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) may offer such a solution and have attracted growing attention for their potential to combat AMR. In parallel, the growing availability of peptide sequences in public databases has stimulated the development of numerous machine learning and deep learning tools to predict antimicrobial activity computationally. However, it remains unclear how reliably these tools can be compared, as existing studies often rely on heterogeneous data sets and inconsistent evaluation protocols that may lead to data leakage and inflated performance estimates. This raises a central question: what evaluation criteria and benchmark resources are needed to enable fair, reproducible, and biologically meaningful assessment of AMP prediction tools? We address this question by focusing specifically on antibacterial peptides (ABPs). We first provide an overview of AMP databases relevant to antibacterial activity and compare their content, redundancy, and experimental metadata. We then critically assess existing computational tools for ABP prediction, highlighting key limitations related to data set construction, affinity to certain sequences, data leakage, and inconsistent performance reporting. Based on these limitations, we propose a reference evaluation framework designed to improve comparability, reproducibility, and practical utility in ABP prediction. Finally, we provide targeted recommendations for AMP databases and future tool development to support more robust progress in the computational discovery of ABPs.

title: Polymer-Derived Tantalum Carbide Ceramic Aerogel Monoliths for Ultrahigh-Temperature Thermal Insulation up to 2000 °C
abstractText: Abstract Ceramic aerogels are ideal thermal insulating materials in the aerospace field because of their low density and low thermal conductivity but are plagued by the limited operating temperature due to the inherently poor high-temperature resistance. In this work, the tantalum carbide (TaC) ceramic aerogel monolith with outstanding ultrahigh temperature stability was successfully prepared through the polymer precursor conversion method combined with the sol–gel technique. Benefiting from the pyrolysis process of the polymer precursor aerogel, the TaC aerogel monoliths with the pearl necklace-like structure were obtained at a low temperature of 1500 °C. The as-prepared TaC aerogels exhibit a low density (0.46–0.63 g/cm3), high Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) specific surface area (95.15–148.17 m2/g), low thermal conductivity (0.046–0.058 W·m–1·K–1), and a good compressive strength (0.043–0.297 MPa). Most importantly, after heat treatment up to 2000 °C under vacuum, the pearl necklace-like structure of the TaC aerogel is well preserved, and the thermal conductivity remains at a low level of 0.059 W·m–1·K–1, indicating the excellent ultrahigh-temperature stability of TaC aerogels. The excellent thermal insulating performance and ultrahigh-temperature stability make the TaC aerogel an attractive material for thermal insulation in extreme conditions.

title: SELF-TUNING FUZZY-PID TECHNIQUE FOR MOBILE MANIPULATOR ROBOT CONSIDERING CENTRAL MASS
abstractText: This research discusses the modeling of a 4-wheel mobile platform equipped with a mounted manipulator and proposes the self-tuning Fuzzy-PID control law for the system. A challenge with a Mobile Manipulator occurs when the manipulator performs tasks while the mobile robot is in motion, which changes the location of the center of mass (CoM) and becomes unstable in control. To address this issue, the dynamics modeling is formulated to account for the CoM displacement effect. This modeling approach estimates the effect of CoM on the motion. Based on this model, a suitable Fuzzy-PID control strategy is designed. This controller can improve the motion efficiency and compare the trajectory of the Mobile Manipulator using a conventional PID controller.

Uncertainty-Quantified Abnormal Detection for Pressure Pipelines Based on Acoustics Hybrid Fusion
abstractText: Abstract With the development of energy and transportation fields, pressure pipelines are being widely used to transport materials, such as natural gas and water. Working at complex conditions and harsh environments over long time periods, pressure pipelines are prone to damage, which affects the safe and stable operation of the transportation system. Based on its advantage of nondestructive testing, acoustic sensors are employed to detect anomalies in a pressure pipeline. However, the detection accuracy is unsatisfactory due to the uncertainty caused by noise interference and minor damage. Therefore, an uncertainty-quantified abnormal detection method is proposed for pressure pipelines, which quantifies and reduces the uncertainty based on acoustic hybrid fusion. Notably, the data-level fusion method is proposed by dividing and fusing raw acoustic signals at low- and high-frequency bands. Further, the 1D convolutional neural network is employed to obtain preliminary results for two raw and data-level fusion acoustic signals. The uncertainty detection results are modified and corrected through the proposed decision-level method, which can achieve accurate abnormal detection of pressure pipelines with high accuracy and reliability. To validate the proposed method, the natural gas and water pressure pipeline experimental platforms are established with noisy and normal environments. The results demonstrate that the propose method can accurately detect anomalies of pressure pipelines with accuracy over 90% for two study cases. It is superior to other methods based on the ablation experiments and comparative results.

title: Klasifikasi Skintone Menggunakan Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) untuk Mencari Persentase Kecocokan dengan Warna Pakaian
abstractText: .. Choosing clothing colors that complement an individual's skin tone often relies on subjective judgment. This study develops a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based system to classify skin tone and calculate clothing color compatibility percentages. A modified MobileNetV2 model was trained on 2,935 facial images categorized into Light, Medium, and Dark classes. Preprocessing included augmentation, normalization, resizing, and face detection using MediaPipe. Model performance was evaluated on an independent test set obtained from Kaggle and separated from training data before model development. The model achieved 94% test accuracy. Following classification, skin color was analyzed in CIELAB and HSV color spaces. Clothing color compatibility was calculated using a weighted scoring method involving five parameters: Hue, Undertone, Value, Saturation, and LAB Distance scores. Compatibility percentages were determined using predefined color-matching criteria. The system was implemented as a web-based application displaying predicted skin tone and compatibility percentages for predefined clothing colors. These findings demonstrate the potential of combining deep learning and color analysis to support more objective and personalized clothing color recommendations.

The Influence of the Socio-Psychological Climate of Higher Educational Institutions on the Formation of Civic Position
abstractText: This study examines how the socio-psychological climate in higher education influences the formation of students’ civic positions across motivational, cognitive, and behavioural components. To address predominantly low-to-medium baseline civic engagement, the study developed and implemented the “Harmony and Citizenship” programme aimed at fostering a supportive educational environment. Effectiveness was evaluated using documentation analysis, pedagogical observation, expert evaluations, and self-assessments. Post-implementation results confirmed the programme’s efficacy, particularly in the experimental group. Behaviourally, the experimental group achieved a higher proportion of high civic engagement (42.7% vs. 41.2% in the control group) and a significant reduction in low-level engagement (13.8% vs. 21.5%). The experimental group also showed gains in high-level motivational (34.1%) and cognitive (33.9%) dimensions. By substantiating key concepts such as civic education, patriotism, and citizenship, this research provides a practical, adaptable methodology for enhancing students’ civic development through institutional climate optimization.

title: Uniform Stability and Optimal Error Estimates of a Difference Finite Element Solution for Three-Dimensional Steady MHD Equations
abstractText: In this paper, a difference finite element (DFE) method is presented for the 3D steady MHD equations. This method approximates the solution pair \(((u,B),p)\) of the 3D steady MHD equations in the \((x,y,z)\)-directions by the DFE solution \[ ((u_h^n,B_h^n),p_h^n)=\left(\sum_{k=0}^{l_3}(u_h^{nk},B_h^{nk})\phi_k(z),\sum_{k=1}^{l_3}p_h^{nk}\psi_k(z)\right) \] of the 3D steady Oseen iterative equations (the 3D steady linearized MHD equations), where \(((u_h^{nk},B_h^{nk}),p_h^{nk})\), based on the finite element space pair \(((P_1^b,P_1^b,P_1),(P_1,P_1,P_1))\times P_1\), is a series of DFE solution pairs for the 2D steady Oseen iterative equations in the \((x,y)\)-directions. Moreover, we prove the existence and uniqueness of the DFE solution \(((u_h^n,B_h^n),p_h^n)\) under the quasi-uniform mesh condition and deduce first-order convergence with respect to \((\sigma^{n+1},\tau,h)\) of the DFE solution \(((u_h^n,B_h^n),p_h^n)\) to the exact solution \(((u,B),p)\). Finally, numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical results and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

Nontraumatic orbital roof blowout fracture following nose blowing: illustrative case
abstractText: BACKGROUND Orbital blowout fractures generally involve the floor or medial wall and usually result from blunt trauma. Nontraumatic orbital roof fractures associated with nose blowing are exceptionally rare. OBSERVATIONS An 84-year-old man developed immediate left orbital swelling, epistaxis, diplopia, and impaired downgaze after forceful nose blowing. CT demonstrated fractures of the left medial orbital wall and orbital roof, with intracranial herniation of orbital tissue. MRI showed herniation of the superior rectus muscle and orbital fat through the roof defect and an adjacent inferior frontal lobe hematoma. During an extradural transcranial operation, herniated orbital fat was found to have penetrated the dura and adhered firmly to the frontal lobe. The adherent tissue was released, the dura and periorbita were repaired, and the orbital roof was reconstructed. Diplopia and downgaze limitation improved postoperatively. LESSONS An orbital roof fracture should be considered when orbital swelling and diplopia develop immediately after forceful nose blowing, even without trauma. Intracranial herniation and adhesion of orbital tissue may contribute to persistent ocular motility disturbance and may warrant surgical treatment. https://thejns.org/doi/abs/10.3171/CASE26847

title: MOLECULAR DOCKING STUDY OF Fe(III) COMPLEXES CONTAINING SALEN-TYPE SCHIFF BASES
abstractText: Our previous work reported the synthesis of Fe(III) complexes containing unsymetrical salen-type Shiff bases from the reaction of 2-hydroxynaphthaldehyde with substituted salicylaldehyde. The cytotoxic activities of these compounds were then evaluated against KB and HepG2 cancer cell lines. The results indicated that Fe(III) complexes exhibited significant anticancer potential, with low IC₅₀ values ranging for both KB and HepG2. To further investigate the binding mode between the ligands and a biological target, molecular docking analysis was performed in this study. Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) tyrosine kinase was chosen as a receptor model because of its relevance to anticancer drug development. The molecular docking results revealed that the stabilization of the Fe(III) complex-receptor was mainly influenced by the nature and position of substituents on the salicylidene moiety. Specifically, among six studied compounds, two high-potency complexes achieved a robust network of 16 interactions, including key salt bridges and attractive charge bonds with Asp831, which were absent in less active derivatives. These findings provide valuable insights into the potential inhibitory mechanisms of the synthesized Fe(III) complexes and support their potential development as novel anticancer agents targeting EGFR.
